title: EngineContract
description: The engine's calls (engine/facade/src/call.rs): for each name, the JSON input it takes and the JSON answer it gives. Generated by wingtip-contract-gen (engine/contract/gen) from each rule's own file beside its code (engine/crates/<crate>/contract/<name>.json, engine/facade/contract/<name>.json) and the types they share (contract/definitions/): change those, not this file. apps/web/src/lib/engine/contract.ts is generated from it (npm run types), and engine/facade/tests/contract.rs holds the engine's answers to it. A member left out of `required` may be missing; a type with null may be null.

acs_codes.description: The ACS codes in pasted text, each once.

ahead_frame.description: Where the data for what is ahead of own ship is wanted (ahead.rs): the box round the five minutes' track, 1 nm wider, for the airspace, special-use areas and TFRs; the box round the next minute's, the swath and half a mile wider, for the FAA's Digital Obstacle File; and the swath's points (the track and 0.25 nm either side, every 2 s) for the ground.

lats.description: Three rows: the track, left of it, right of it.

airborne_now.description: Whether a watched airplane is in the air: true, false, or null where not known.

aircraft_problems.description: What is wrong with the "Your Airplane" form's fields as typed, by field (the gateway's AircraftRequest names), in the words shown under each; {} where it may be saved. Tail number and type designator required, at most 16 characters (the columns'); cruise speed and burn positive numbers, the climb's and usable fuel blank or positive; cruise power blank or 40 to 100%; equipment and surveillance letters and figures, at most 40 and 20 (FAA Form 7233-4 items 10a and 10b, AIM Appendix 4, TBL 4-2 and 4-3); colour at most 40 characters.

airplane_figures.description: An airplane's figures, each with where it comes from: its pilot's own where they differ from the book's ("pilot"), else its photographed handbook page's ("handbook"), else its type's stock profile's ("book"); a figure none has is null, never another airplane's (the owner, 2026-11-09). The empty weight and moment are the pilot's alone (a stock profile's are its handbook's sample airplane's). `profile` is the book's with the picked figures over it, the airplane every other rule takes; null with no book, handbook or own figures (no airplane).

book.description: The type's stock profile (the planner's /api/aircraft-profiles entry); null for a type with none.

handbook.description: The figures its pilot confirmed off a photographed handbook page (handbook_figures' answer); null for none.

own.description: The pilot's own figures by key (cruise_tas_kt, glide_ratio ...), a number or null each; null for none.

key.description: The figure's name, the gateway record's and the planner's query's in snake case.

source.description: Where the value comes from; null where there is none.

book.description: The type's book figure, what "Reset to book figure" puts back; null where the book has none.

airplane_needs.description: The inputs a figure needs that the airplane's profile lacks, by name, so the app asks for them where the figure would be (the owner, 2026-11-09): the legs their cruise speed and burn; the fuel totals also the start, taxi and takeoff allowance; the glide its glide ratio; the climb its climb speed, sea-level rate and service ceiling; a weight and balance its loading envelope and its own empty weight and moment; takeoff and landing their charts. ["airplane"] with no airplane.

profile.description: The airplane (airplane_figures' profile); null for no airplane.

missing.description: The inputs' names in order: a figure's key (taxi_fuel_gal, glide_ratio ...), a table (loading, takeoff, landing), or airplane.

airspace_column.description: The airspace over a point in bands, from the ground to FL600 (14 CFR 71.33, 71.71): a B, C or D where it is drawn, the most restrictive where they overlap, E from its floor or 14,500 ft, G under it all, A from 18,000 ft, split where 91.155's minimums, 91.117's speed or 91.215's transponder rule changes. The volumes are the caller's, read from the NASR shapefile or a cycle pack.

in_veil.description: Inside a 30 nm Mode C veil (91.215(b)(2)).

airspace_entry_rules.description: A Class B, C or D's entry, equipment and speed rules (14 CFR 91.117, 91.129-91.131, 91.215, 91.225), each with its cite, and whom to call. Any other one-letter class answers no rules.

class.description: One letter: B, C or D.

call.description: The frequency types to call: TWR for a Class D, APP then TWR otherwise.

airway_floor_ft.description: An airway segment's minimum IFR altitude (14 CFR 91.177(a)(1)): its MEA, else its GNSS MEA; null where it publishes neither.

alert_fires.description: Whether a watched airplane's alert goes off now: takes off, lands, or comes within limit_nm of a place.

inside.description: Near something: whether it is that near now; null for the others.

bearing_deg.description: True bearing from the place to the airplane.

alerts_ahead.description: What is ahead of own ship from the planner's data (ahead.rs): the Class B, C and D (91.129-91.131), special-use areas (91.133, AIM 3-4) and TFRs (91.137-91.145, 99.7) its track goes into in the next five minutes, and the ground or a DOF obstacle it comes within 500 ft of in the next minute (borrowed from 91.119(c)); warnings first, then the soonest. Nothing under 40 kt. Advisory: not a TAWS (TSO-C151). A list given as null was not read, and is named in `unavailable`.

type.description: P, R, MOA, W or A.

ground_ft.description: The ground under the area, for AGL heights.

swath_ground_ft.description: The ground at ahead_frame's swath, its rows.

ground_ft.description: The ground under the airplane as given (ground_ft), or null: the member the phones' answer from the packs carries too, which their glide ring stands on (#218).

altitude_advisor.description: The Altitude Advisor's rows, highest first: the altitude wheel's (the legal altitudes, the one flown, every 500 ft from 1,000 ft to 17,500 ft under Class A, 14 CFR 71.33, 91.135), each with the route's time, fuel and head or tail wind where the planner has them; Fastest (the winds') and Most economical (the fuel's, climbs included) marked from the planner's plans, else the legal row with the least time and fuel; a row outside the legal altitudes (91.119, 91.159, 91.179, airspace, clouds, the ceiling) kept with a warning (the owner's warn, never limit).

altitude_allowed.description: Whether an altitude asked for may be planned: at least 500 ft (91.119(c)), under Class A for VFR (any figure under 18,000 ft MSL, 71.33(a), 91.135), at most FL410 for IFR (91.179(b)(4)).

altitude_anyway.description: The altitude a route with no legal one is flown at anyway (the owner's warn, never limit): the lowest over the floor everywhere on the course's own altitudes (14 CFR 91.159, 91.179(b)); null where no floor is known.

altitude_change.description: A pilot's own change of altitude at a waypoint: Start At (begins at the waypoint) or Cross At (done by it), where along the route it begins and ends, its gradient, and with an airplane its minutes and gallons. The climb is the airplane's best-rate climb, slower the thinner the air (PHAK ch. 11), over the ground at its climb speed scaled by the leg's wind; the descent the nav log's three to one (about a 3 degree path, AIM 2-1-2) at the leg's ground speed and burn. No airplane: no time or fuel, the descent's geometry alone, and a climb drawn as a step.

profile.description: The picked airplane's profile, the same one the nav log takes (NavLogProfile: its cruise_tas_kt, fuel_burn_gph and service_ceiling_ft, and for a climb climb_tas_kt, climb_rate_fpm_sea_level and climb_fuel_burn_gph, wingtip_flight::performance). A climb's ground, minutes and gallons come from its climb figures; with none of them (no climb_tas_kt) the climb is drawn as a step. Null or left out where no airplane is picked: nothing is assumed (the owner, 2026-11-09), a descent keeps its geometry and has no time or fuel.

along_nm.description: Where the waypoint is along the route, nautical miles from the departure.

from_ft.description: The altitude flown into the waypoint, feet MSL.

to_ft.description: The waypoint's own altitude, feet MSL.

mode.description: start_at: the change begins at the waypoint and runs on from it; cross_at: it is done by the waypoint.

groundspeed_kt.description: The leg's ground speed, knots: a descent's minutes, and with tas_kt the wind a climb's ground speed is scaled by. Null where the leg has none.

tas_kt.description: The leg's cruise true airspeed, knots, for the wind's share of the ground speed.

fuel_burn_gph.description: The leg's cruise burn, gallons an hour: a descent's gallons.

oat_c.description: The forecast temperature at to_ft, degrees C: the climb is flown that far from a standard day (ISA, PHAK ch. 4). Null for a standard day.

altitude_limits.description: The altitudes a flight may be planned at: no lower than 500 ft (14 CFR 91.119(c)), VFR up to 17,500 ft (91.159(a)'s highest under Class A, which begins at 18,000 ft MSL, 71.33(a), and takes IFR only, 91.135), IFR up to FL410 (the highest 91.179(b)(4) names); flight levels from 18,000 ft (91.121(a)(2)); 91.159's cruising altitudes 500 ft apart.

altitude_lines.description: A fix's altitude restriction as the chart draws it: the kind of crossing, and each figure underlined (at or above) or overlined (at or below).

altitude_said.description: An altitude as ATC says it and the app writes it (AIM 4-2-9): feet below 18,000 ft ("5,500 ft"), a flight level from there up ("FL180"; 14 CFR 91.121(a)(2)).

altitude_wheel.description: The altitude wheel's rows, highest first: the legal altitudes given, the one flown, and every 500 ft from 1,000 ft to 17,500 ft under Class A (14 CFR 71.33, 91.135) besides (the owner's pick, 2026-10-20).

approach_along_nm.description: How far along a path a place is, nm.

approach_attempts.description: The attempts at the approach in a track, as point indices.

approach_brief.description: The approach briefed, item by item.

approach_category.description: The approach category (14 CFR 97.3) from VREF, or 1.3 VSO, or null with neither.

approach_coaching.description: The approach flown fix by fix, with a word at each.

approach_debrief.description: One attempt at an approach debriefed, or null.

approach_descent_fpm.description: The descent rate on the path, ft/min (the TPP's rate of descent table).

approach_find.description: The approaches a track flew, each debriefed.

approach_fix_tags.description: The tags an approach's fixes carry on the map with its plate, ForeFlight's way: each fix's crossing altitude and its sense (ARINC 424-18 5.29); at the final approach fix the ILS's glide slope altitude as the CIFP codes it, or an LPV or LNAV/VNAV approach's glidepath altitude worked out from its angle, threshold and TCH (FAA Order 8260.3G formula 2-6-4); at a runway missed approach point its threshold crossing height and touchdown zone elevation (no DA or MDA: the minimums are the plate's alone); and the final approach segment, FAF to MAP.

final.description: The final approach segment, from the FAF to the MAP, for the map to mark.

approach_guidance.description: How the approach is flown, by its CIFP id (ARINC 424-18 5.10): "localizer", "gps" or "other".

approach_lesson_path.description: The lesson's line, the way in to the runway.

approach_minimums.description: The findings held to the pilot's minimums (14 CFR 91.175(c), (e)).

approach_path_between.description: The part of a path between two places on it.

approach_profile.description: The approach seen from the side: its fixes along the way in and the path down from the final approach fix.

approach_quiz.description: The approach asked back as a quiz; answer is the index of the right choice.

approach_transition.description: The transition's debrief, or null, from the vectors' debrief's figures.

arrival_circuit.description: The arrival's circuit as the planner draws it, or null.

atc_call.description: A transmission heard by the ATC copilot: who said it, by our call sign's place (AIM 4-2-3 c, 4-2-4), and its items in the order said (AIM 4-4-7 b.2).

awc_airsigmets_read.description: The Aviation Weather Center's national airsigmets cache file (XML) read into the shape the weather store keeps: [{hazard, type, altitude_low_ft, altitude_high_ft, raw, valid_from, valid_to, issued, coords}].

awc_gairmets_read.description: The Aviation Weather Center's national gairmets cache file (XML) read into the shape the weather store keeps: The G-AIRMET areas a VFR flight is told of: [{hazard (words), severity, due_to, valid_at, valid, issued, altitude_low_ft, from_freezing_level, altitude_high_ft, coords}].

awc_metars_read.description: The Aviation Weather Center's national metars cache file (XML) read into the shape the weather store keeps: {ident: report}, the newest per station: its text, time, flight category (only what the visibility settles where the ceiling is not known), ceiling (14 CFR 1.1) and its layer's cover, visibility, wind, altimeter, temperature and dewpoint, and where it is.

additionalProperties.title: AwcMetar
additionalProperties.description: A station's newest METAR as the weather store keeps it.

ceiling_cover.description: The ceiling layer's cover as a METAR writes the ceiling (OVC008, VV002; FMH-1 ch. 9): BKN, OVC or VV for an obscuration; null with no ceiling or one of unknown height.

awc_pireps_read.description: The Aviation Weather Center's national pireps cache file (XML) read into the shape the weather store keeps: The PIREPs (UA, UUA), not the AIREPs: [{observed_at, observed, lat, lon, altitude_ft, aircraft, urgent, turbulence, icing, raw}].

awc_tafs_read.description: The Aviation Weather Center's national tafs cache file (XML) read into the shape the weather store keeps: [{icaoId, lat, lon, elevation_ft, raw, fcsts}], each station's latest TAF, its periods in time order.

bare_field.description: A field's FAA ident (the K of a US ICAO code left off).

bearing_deg.description: The initial great-circle course from the first point to the second, degrees true 0 to 360, on the same sphere as distance_nm (wingtip.geo.bearing_deg); 0 for two points that coincide.

below_vfr_minimums.description: Whether a ceiling or a visibility is under 14 CFR 91.155(c), (d)'s basic VFR minimums (1,000 ft, 3 sm); a missing figure is below nothing.

best_fields.description: The best fields to land at from where the airplane is, ranked with their reasons: in "glide" mode (the engine stopped) by reach first -- over the field at pattern height, reachable lower, beyond -- with the airplane's best-glide figures and the wind aloft, then the runway against the POH and the distance; in "diversion" mode by the runway and the weather, then the time. With no glide figures the glide is not guessed: nearest first, needs_airplane true. Nothing is left out for a limitation; it is said and ranked lower. A glide ratio with no best-glide speed gives a reach only with no wind aloft: a headwind's loss needs the glide's airspeed, and a still-air reach into one would be too far.

speed_kt.description: Groundspeed; under 40 kt the airplane is taken to be on the ground.

wind.description: The wind at the airplane's altitude, true.

glide.description: The POH's best-glide speed and glide ratio (Section 3).

best_glide_kias.description: The POH's best-glide speed, indicated; null or missing where the profile has none (a pilot's own airplane given its glide ratio alone): the reach is then worked only in still air: with a wind aloft it is not (a headwind's loss cannot be worked without the airspeed), and the fields are ranked as with no glide.

limit.description: At most this many; 10 where not given.

needs_airplane.description: Glide mode with no best-glide figures: ranked by distance alone.

tas_kt.description: The true airspeed at best glide; null with no best-glide speed.

ring.description: The ground the glide reaches every 10 degrees, wind corrected, [lat, lon].

call_pattern.description: Our call sign as a regular expression over a recognizer's words (AIM 4-2-4), for a locked phone's listener; null where `tail` is no registration.

ceiling_ft.description: A report's ceiling, ft above the ground: the lowest broken, overcast or obscured layer (14 CFR 1.1), an obscured sky's at its vertical visibility; null where there is none or it is not known (sky_ceiling tells them apart).

ceiling_visibility.description: A report's or a forecast group's ceiling (14 CFR 1.1: the lowest broken or overcast layer, or the vertical visibility into an obscuration) and its visibility in statute miles, from the groups a host's own reader found: metres converted as the engine's METAR reader converts them (9999 the AWC's 6+), to the hundredth; CAVOK 6 (WMO No. 306: 10 km or more). Each null where none is given.

cover.description: As a METAR codes it: FEW, SCT, BKN, OVC, VV; others count for no ceiling.

checklist_phases.description: The headings a checklist can start from, with nothing under them: a pilot's operating handbook's Normal Procedures (GAMA Specification No. 1, Section 4) or Emergency Procedures (Section 3), in its order; the items are the pilot's, from their own airplane's handbook (FAA-H-8083-3C, chapter 2).

checklist_read.description: A checklist typed as text read into its sections, each with its items' challenge and response, as the apps keep and show it.

checklist_section.description: Which of a checklist's section titles is the emergency `want` ("Engine failure in flight" where not given, one of the emergency phases, GAMA Specification No. 1, Section 3), as the pilot wrote it: the one sharing the most of its words, at least two; null where none does.

checklist_write.description: A checklist written as text again: each section its "# title" line and its items, "challenge -- response".

checkpoints_select.description: The nav log's checkpoints from the chart model's scored candidates, as their indices in route order: greedy by score, at least `min_spacing_nm` apart (10), none under `min_score` (2.5; null for every score), at most `max_count`, and with `length_nm` none within 3 nm of a hop's ends.

class_b_detours.description: Named fixes to fly through so neither leg comes within a mile of the Class B whose floor is under below_ft (route/options/classb.rs): those adding the least distance first, a VFR waypoint before a GPS fix that saves under 10 nm, at most 5, none adding over 40 nm.

class_b_entered.description: Whether a straight leg flown at altitude_ft enters Class B (route/options/classb.rs): a shelf whose floor is at or under it and whose ceiling at or over it, which the leg goes into (14 CFR 91.131(a): an ATC clearance before entering). Under a shelf or over the top, it does not.

cleared_route.description: The route a clearance gives, from the words heard, the planner's places found for them (ClearancePlaces) and the route planned.

closest_approach.description: When and how near an airplane comes to own ship, both carried on straight, within 10 minutes; null without both tracks and speeds.

above_ft.description: Its height above own ship's then, ft.

cloud_clearance_at_ft.description: The distance 14 CFR 91.155(a) keeps below the clouds at an altitude: 1,000 ft at or above 10,000 ft MSL, 500 ft below.

compass_word.description: A bearing as one of the eight compass points.

congested_points.description: Whether each point is over a congested area or within 2,000 ft of one (14 CFR 91.119(b)'s 'horizontal radius of 2,000 feet'), east-west by the cosine of the point's latitude, from the towns the planner reads (Census urban areas and gazetteer places).

candidates.description: For each point, the indices of the areas to measure it against; null, all of them.

copilot_watch.description: The in-flight copilot: from own ship and the live data, the messages that change what the pilot should do, most pressing first (warning, caution, advisory; then the kinds' order), each with the words to show and speak and its sources. Warns, never limits.

csv_rows.description: A CSV file's rows of fields.

ctaf_of.description: The CTAF's index in frequencies (a CTAF, else a UNICOM that is the CTAF, else a UNICOM), or MULTICOM's 122.9 as a frequency where none is listed (AC 90-66C 9.6).

data_cycle.description: Whether an FAA data set's edition is in force on a day, by its cycle: AIRAC's 28 days (NASR, CIFP, d-TPP), the 56-day charting cycle (sectional, terminal area and IFR enroute charts, the Chart Supplement) or the Digital Obstacle File's 56-day releases, from the FAA's 28 and 56 Day Product Schedule and its DOF page.

kind.description: The schedule the data set is published on.

effective.description: YYYY-MM-DD: the date the edition held is named by (its effective date; a DOF file's last day of changes). Missing or null where nothing says.

on.description: YYYY-MM-DD: the UTC day it is used on.

current.description: YYYY-MM-DD: the day the edition in force on `on` took effect (a DOF's release).

current_ident.description: The AIRAC cycle's number, YYNN ("2611"); null off AIRAC.

next.description: YYYY-MM-DD: the day the next edition takes its place.

effective.description: YYYY-MM-DD: the day the edition held counts from; null where unknown.

expires.description: YYYY-MM-DD: the first day the edition held no longer counts; null where unknown.

behind.description: How many editions have come out since the one held; 0 unless expired.

debrief.description: The planner's /api/debrief answer (ACS PA.VI.A): the flight flown against the plan, each finding marked, and the tolerances it is held to.

anyOf.description: Each field's pattern altitude, ft MSL, by ident.

debrief_airborne.description: The track's flights as [first, last] point indices.

debrief_marked.description: The web's debrief (its figures, snake_case, no marks) marked against ACS PA.VI.A's tolerances as `debrief` marks its own, with the tolerances.

debrief.description: The debrief's figures as `debrief` gives them, unmarked: legs, passes, patterns and the rest.

density_altitude_ft.description: The altitude at which a standard day's air has density sigma.

density_ratio.description: Sigma, the air's density at a pressure altitude and temperature over a standard day's at sea level (ICAO Doc 7488).

departure_circuit.description: The departure's circuit and the course out, or null.

departure_pattern.description: The pattern to leave an end, toward a place where given, or null.

departure_window.description: "When should I go?": the Go / No-Go for each departure hour the forecasts reach (the Brief's findings, the IFR alternate's say and the risk assessment with the hour's night, 14 CFR 1.1 and 61.57(b)), each go, caution, no-go or unknown with the one or two findings that decide it, and the runs of go hours ranked best first: the most margin over the minimums, then the shortest ETE.

start.description: The departure, [lat, lon]: the night is judged along the straight line to `end`.

airplane.description: An airplane is picked: without one the fuel, the runways and the weight and balance are left out, ETE and fuel are null, and the night is judged at the departure alone.

minimums.description: The pilot's own ceiling and visibility minimums, which the margin is counted against; 14 CFR 91.155(c), (d)'s 1,000 ft and 3 sm where one is not set.

risk.description: The risk assessment's input as the Go / No-Go sends it; its briefing and nav log members (vfr_not_recommended, under_minimums, tfr_on_route, hazards, night, night_passengers, fuel_margin_gal) are each hour's own. Null: no assessment, as with no briefing.

reaches.description: The forecasts reach the whole flight; false, the hour is unknown.

ground_min.description: Minutes on the ground at the stops, counted in the night's span.

ceiling_ft.description: The forecast's lowest ceiling along the route for this flight; null, none.

reasons.description: The one or two findings that decide it; for a go, the weather's.

night.description: Any of the flight at night (14 CFR 1.1).

night_passengers.description: Any of it in 14 CFR 61.57(b)'s night-passenger period.

margin.description: The forecast's worst along the route over the minimums, the lesser ratio of ceiling and visibility, at most 3.

windows.description: The runs of go hours, best first.

quickest_s.description: The departure hour in it with the shortest ETE.

destination.description: Where a great circle from each point on its true course reaches its distance out, on the same sphere as distance_nm, the longitude within -180 to 180: the phones' traffic carried on along its track between reports, a list so a map's airplanes cross once.

diagram_fix_usable.description: Whether own ship is drawn on the airport diagram: a fix no older than 3 s (AC 120-76D 11.17.2.3) and good to 30 m or better (11.17.2.4); a negative accuracy, none known, never.

diagram_graticule.description: How an airport diagram's page matches the ground, from its latitude and longitude labels placed on the page (points from its top left): the coordinate along lat_on_x's axis is a * lat + b, along the other c * lon + d; north_deg which way north points, clockwise from the page's top. Null with fewer than two of either, their scales more than 15% apart, or a mirrored page (wingtip.publications _graticule's check).

diagram_labels.description: The latitude and longitude labels in an FAA airport diagram's page text ("46°51'N", "92°13'W"), each once, as written, for the app to find where each is drawn.

diagram_point.description: Where a point on the ground is on an airport diagram's page by its graticule, points from the top left, and whether it is on the page.

direct_of.description: The place a "direct" sends us to, as words to find, or null.

distance_nm.description: The great-circle distance between two points, nm, on the sphere of 3,440.065 nm flight computers use (wingtip.geo, pyproj's Geod with f = 0), the great circle of FAA-H-8083-25C ch. 16.

diversion.description: The planner's /api/diversion solved, steps, problem and checks (ACS PA.VI.C): the diversion worked out in the leg's own air, and the student's estimates checked against it.

to.description: The field's ident, for the problem's words.

diversion_reasonable.description: Whether a student's estimate is within the diversion drill's allowance (ACS PA.VI.C.S2); an error for a key not estimated.

drill_decks.description: The oral's flash cards in the regulation's words: the tower's light signals (14 CFR 91.125) on the ground and in flight, and the basic VFR weather minimums (91.155(a), worded from the airspace column's own table; Class A from 91.135, the night pattern exception 91.155(b)(2)).

drill_next.description: A flash card answered, by Leitner's boxes: known, up a box (a card never seen counts as the first) to the fifth at most; missed, back to the first. Its new box and the days until it is due again: 0, 1, 3, 7 and 16 for boxes 1 to 5.

dry_run.description: The planned flight flown on paper along the nav log's rows, by its procedures and holds, going missed when asked.

due_tone.description: How near a paperwork item falls due, as every app colours its row: past is a stop, within 30 days (the reminders' first email, the gateway's ReminderService) or 10 hours of time in service a caution, further off ok; unknown with neither. By its day where it has one, else its hours.

emergency_guidance.description: What to do in an emergency with no airplane picked: general good practice only, each item with its source -- fly the airplane and pick a field within reach (FAA-H-8083-3C ch. 18), ask for help early (AIM 6-1-2), squawk 7700 (AIM 6-2-2), MAYDAY on the frequency in use or 121.5 (AIM 6-3-1, 6-3-2), climb if possible (AIM 6-3-2), stay in VFR conditions and the pilot in command's authority to deviate (AIM 6-2-1, 6-1-1, 14 CFR 91.3(b)). No airplane's checklist, speeds, glide or distances.

source.description: Where it comes from: the AIM paragraph, the handbook's chapter or the CFR section.

emitter_category.description: An ADS-B emitter category's name in DO-260B's words (GDL 90 Table 11): A1 to A7 and B1, B2; null for one not sent and for the rest.

endorsement_fill.description: An endorsement filled in to sign (AC 61-65K appendix A): the fields it takes, each tidied to single spaces and "" where not given, any it does not take left out; the labels of the required ones still empty; and its words with the student and the fields in, as endorsement_render fills them. Null for a code no endorsement has.

endorsement_kinds.description: The endorsements a student meets on the way to a private pilot certificate, in the order they meet them: AC 61-65K appendix A's sample for each (November 2025), word for word, with the 14 CFR section it answers. A template names the student {student} and each blank by its field's key.

template.description: The sample's words, {student} and each field's {key} in them.

endorsement_lapse.description: The warning an instructor sees once their date has passed on the day of signing (14 CFR 61.197(a), (e)), or null.

until_kind.description: "EXP" for the certificate's expiry; anything else is recent experience ("RE").

endorsement_records.description: What a student's endorsements say: each one's last good day (90 days for a solo endorsement, 14 CFR 61.87(n), (p), the night solo's, 61.87(o), and Class B's, 61.95(a)(2), (b)(2); AC 61-65K A.5-A.7, A.12, A.13; null for one that does not run out), the day their solo endorsement runs out, and, for a solo cross-country on flight_on, what their record answers of 61.93(d): (4) a solo cross-country endorsement (61.93(c)(1), (2)) and (5) a solo endorsement within the 90 days before the flight.

endorsement_render.description: An endorsement's words as they will be signed.

endorsements_in_force.description: The latest not voided of each code, as [code, index] into the record (newest first).

endurance.description: An airplane's endurance from its own figures: its usable fuel over its cruise burn, minutes, and the minutes left once the reserve is kept back -- 30 minutes at normal cruise by day and 45 at night under VFR (14 CFR 91.151(a)), 45 under IFR (91.167(a)(3)), or none. The reserve's fuel at the burn, gallons. Below the reserve the minutes left are 0 and below_reserve is true: a warning, never a refusal. Null where the airplane gives no usable fuel or no burn; never a stock airplane's figures.

usable_gal.description: The airplane's usable fuel, gallons (its profile's); null or missing where it has none.

burn_gph.description: The airplane's cruise burn, gallons an hour (its profile's); null or missing where it has none.

reserve.description: The reserve kept back: vfr_day (30 min, 91.151(a)(1)), vfr_night (45 min, 91.151(a)(2)), ifr (45 min, 91.167(a)(3)) or none.

faa_ids.description: The FAA identifiers an airport may go by in NASR (KSTL and STL).

faa_words.description: The FAA's capitals in sentence case, its codes kept (AIM 3-2-1's "Class B"; an approach's title as AIM 5-4-5 names it, "ILS or LOC rwy 36"): one string from text, or each of texts as a list (a null row answers "").

texts.description: A long list's rows in one call; where given, text is not read.

field_hours.description: A field's weather hour by hour for the airport card: Now from the METAR, then each whole hour its TAF covers, the TAF's change groups read as FAA-H-8083-28B 27.4.2.10 sets them out (a BECMG under way the worse of before and after, a TEMPO's or PROB's worse weather at times).

metar.description: The field's report as the planner gives it.

count.description: Hours after Now; 24 where not given.

field_relation.description: Whether an airplane is around a field, inbound to it or departing it.

field_taf.description: The TAF that speaks for a field: its own (the station whose ICAO id is the ident, or K and a three-letter ident), else the nearest within 25 nm, the planner's reach past a TAF's 5 sm and 10 sm vicinity (FAA-H-8083-28B 27.4.1, 24.4.3.8.2).

at.description: Where the field is; null where it is not known (its own TAF only).

index.description: The station's index in `stations`; null for none within reach.

nm.description: How far the nearest is; null for the field's own.

reach_nm.description: How far a TAF is taken to speak for a field without its own.

fields_along.description: The public fields along a route for the map's Stops (route/options/fuel.rs): those on a paved runway of 2,500 ft no more than 30 nm off each flight's line, not the route's own, each on the first flight it is near with its miles from that flight's departure and the miles it adds; the 40 nearest the line, in route order.

filed_dof.description: Item 18's date of flight, DOF/YYMMDD, where the flight is not on the UTC day it is filed (AIM Appendix 4, TBL 4-1); null on the same day.

filed_duration.description: Hours and minutes in four figures, HHMM, as items 16 (total EET) and 19 (endurance) of FAA Form 7233-4 take them (AIM Appendix 4), the minutes rounded first; the caller rounds the time en route up and the endurance down.

filed_endurance.description: Item 19's endurance in whole minutes: the fuel aboard at the cruise burn, to the minute below (AIM Appendix 4); null where the burn is not a positive figure.

filed_level.description: The level in item 15 of the flight plan (FAA Form 7233-4, AIM Appendix 4): "F" and three figures, a flight level, at and above 18,000 ft (14 CFR 91.121(a)(2)); "A" and the hundreds of feet in three figures below it ("F350", "A080").

filed_rnav.description: Whether item 15's route takes a T or Q route, an RNAV route (AIM 5-3-4), which asks for G and R in item 10a and PBN/C2 in item 18 where the airplane has them (AIM Appendix 4, TBL 4-13).

filed_route.description: Item 15's route between the departure and the destination (AIM Appendix 4: "DALL3 EIC V18 MEI LGC4", "FLACK DCT IRW"): airways between the fixes they are joined and left at, DCT between two fixes flown direct, a departure procedure first with its transition's fix, an arrival last after its transition's fix; DCT alone for a flight direct. `airways` names which of the stops are airways.

filed_speed.description: Item 15's cruising speed on FAA Form 7233-4: the true airspeed in knots, "N" and four figures (AIM Appendix 4: "N0450").

filed_wake.description: Item 9's wake turbulence category: "L" for a maximum certificated takeoff weight of 15,500 lb or less (AIM Appendix 4, from FAA Order JO 7360.1), null where the weight is not known or is more.

filed_zzzz.description: Whether a field's identifier has a figure in it (C81, 06A) and so no ICAO four-letter location indicator: filed as ZZZZ with its name in item 18 (DEP/, DEST/, ALTN/; AIM Appendix 4) where a service takes only indicators.

fix_radial_distance.description: A point as a fix-radial-distance off the nearest station with a variation, "JOT 045° 12 nm" (AIM 5-1-6), or null.

flight_category.description: A field's flight category (AIM 7-1-7); with no visibility, LIFR only under a 500 ft ceiling and else null.

ceiling_unknown.description: The lowest broken, overcast or obscured layer was sent with no height (OVC///): the ceiling is not known, and only a visibility under a mile says the category (14 CFR 1.1).

floor_caution.description: What a leg flown at an altitude breaks of 14 CFR 91.119 under VFR, in a pilot's words (1,000 ft within 2,000 ft over a congested area, 91.119(b); 500 ft elsewhere, (c)); null where it keeps it.

segment.description: A selection's segment: floor_ft, highest_ft, highest_is_obstacle, obstacle_type, obstacle_clearance_ft, congested.

forecast_hour.description: The winds period for a departure hours ahead: 06 to six hours, 12 to fifteen, 24 beyond (the FB's FOR USE windows, FAA-H-8083-28B Table 27-2).

forecast_run.description: The dry run played against the forecast: for each point of the run (its time, place and altitude), the forecast ceiling and visibility then (the TAF that speaks for it, within 25 nm, and the NWS Gridded LAMP's hour, the worse of the two), the winds aloft at its altitude from the GFS period for that time, and the SIGMETs, G-AIRMET snapshots (90 minutes either side) and SPC Day 1 convective outlook areas over it then; each leg's worst flight category (AIM 7-1-7); each landing's TAF from an hour before to an hour after it is in (14 CFR 91.169(a)(2)'s window) and the departure's an hour on; and an alert, cited, where it first meets forecast weather under 14 CFR 91.155's VFR minimums (flown VFR; Class C, D and E's figures and 91.155(c)'s 1,000 ft ceiling held throughout, the safer reading) or under the pilot's own, or enters an advisory area. Warned, never refused.

track.description: The run's points, in time order.

row.description: The nav log's row the airplane is flying to: its leg.

modelled.description: The Gridded LAMP's forecast hours at this point.

winds.description: Each GFS period's winds at the station nearest this point.

tafs.description: TAF stations as the weather store keeps them.

outlooks.description: SPC outlook areas: {label, valid_from, valid_to, coords}.

category.description: AIM 7-1-7's flight category; null where the forecast does not settle it.

source.description: Whose forecast it is: "TAF KMSN", "TAF KMSN, 12 nm away" or "NWS Gridded LAMP, modelled for 1500Z".

category.description: AIM 7-1-7's flight category; null where the forecast does not settle it.
AIM 7-1-7's flight category; null where the forecast does not settle it.

source.description: Whose forecast it is: "TAF KMSN", "TAF KMSN, 12 nm away" or "NWS Gridded LAMP, modelled for 1500Z".
The rule and the product it is held to.

frd_near.description: A point named as the pilot's own point off the nearest fix a pilot knows (a navaid or a VFR waypoint) within max_nm (40 by default), else the nearest of any kind: its course magnetic, a VOR's radial by the station's own variation (AIM 1-1-3), any other by the World Magnetic Model's at now_s, to the degree, and its distance to a tenth of a mile; null with no fix near.

frd_read.description: A fix-radial-distance point read from text, or null.

freezing_level.description: Where a temperature profile crosses 0 C, by linear interpolation; at_or_below where it is already freezing at the lowest level; null where it stays above freezing.

frequency_line.description: A field's frequency as its card lists it: its name in words, its kind for the row's glyph, and the description in sentence case where that adds to the name.

frequency_of.description: The index of the first frequency (with a MHz) of the first of types the field lists, or null.

fuel_estimate.description: The figures from the airplane's book alone, before the nav log's: at cruise speed with no wind the minutes over the distance, the fuel at the cruise burn over them, and the fuel required, that with the airplane's own start and taxi allowance (taxi_fuel_gal, its profile's; left out where it has none, never a stock airplane's) and 45 minutes' reserve at the cruise burn, the most the rules ask (14 CFR 91.151(a)(2), 91.167(a)(3)), so an estimate is never short of a reserve. Null where the book gives no speed, or no burn for the fuel.

taxi_fuel_gal.description: The airplane's own fuel for engine start, taxi and takeoff, gallons (its profile's taxi_fuel_gal); null or missing for none.

fuel_in_tanks.description: The fuel in the tanks at each point of the route and whether it is under the reserve: full at the departure, the start, taxi and takeoff allowance and each leg's burn taken from them after, filled again at each field landed at, as the planner checks each flight; null at a point past a leg whose burn is not known, until the next fill.

fuel_gal.description: The burn of the leg to it.

refuel.description: The tanks filled on landing there.

fuel_names.description: A field's fuel codes (NASR's) as names.

fuel_stops.description: The fuel stops a flight too long for its tanks needs (route/options/fuel.rs): the fields with fuel no more than 30 nm off its line on a paved runway of 2,500 ft, chained so every landing keeps the reserve (14 CFR 91.151(a), 91.167(a)(3)) at the flight's own burn and minutes a mile, the tanks filled at each, the quickest trip with ground_min (30) a stop, among first stops within 5 minutes of it the one nearest the line then the one whose landings keep the most fuel, at most 8 stops; and up to 4 other first stops. Both empty where none is needed or no field reaches.

gairmet_hazards.description: The G-AIRMET hazards a VFR flight is told of, code to words, and how near some time of the flight a snapshot (three hours apart) is told, seconds (FAA-H-8083-28B 26.3.1.1).

gairmets_along_route.description: The G-AIRMET snapshots whose area the route crosses, valid within 90 minutes of some time of the flight (FAA-H-8083-28B 26.3.1.1).

glide_range.description: Still-air glide range, nm, at the picked airplane's own glide ratio (glide_ratio: feet forward for each foot down, its POH's Section 3 maximum glide, as its profile gives it), or null on the ground, with no height, or with no glide ratio: no airplane, or none in its profile, has no glide worked out.

glide_ratio.description: The airplane's still-air glide ratio, feet forward for each foot down (its profile's glide.ratio); null or missing for none.

glide_reaches.description: Whether a field distance_nm off is within still-air glide, arriving at pattern height (AC 90-66C's 1,000 ft), at the picked airplane's own glide_ratio; false with no glide ratio (no airplane, or none in its profile).

glide_ratio.description: The airplane's still-air glide ratio, feet forward for each foot down (its profile's glide.ratio); null or missing for none.

glide_ring.description: The still-air glide ring about own ship (#218): glide_range's radius at the picked airplane's own glide_ratio over the higher of the ground under the airplane (a pack's terrain) and the nearest field's elevation, and its outline as 73 points on the sphere, the first repeated last. Null on the ground, under flying speed, with no height, or with no glide ratio (no airplane, or none in its profile).

glide_ratio.description: The airplane's still-air glide ratio, feet forward for each foot down (its profile's glide.ratio); null or missing for none.

gonogo_alternate_finding.description: What the IFR alternate comes to for the Go / No-Go (14 CFR 91.169(a)(2), (b)): a stop where the one filed will not do, a caution where one is needed and none is filed or it is the pilot's to check; null where none is needed.

gonogo_balance.description: Weight and balance at takeoff and landing, against the profile's limits and envelope, with the problems found.

arm_in.description: null where the weight is zero.
null where the weight is zero.

gonogo_default_load.description: The load a profile starts with: its sample empty weight and arm, stations empty, the fuel given.

stations_lb.description: 170 lb at the first station, 0 at the others.

gonogo_density_altitude.description: Density altitude, ft, from pressure altitude and temperature (PHAK ch. 4).

gonogo_end_distance.description: The distances on a runway and whether they are over its length.

caveats.description: What could not be had from the table: beyond its altitudes or temperatures, heavier than its heaviest weight, a tailwind past the POH's figures, or no wind correction in the airplane's profile.

gonogo_hazard_window.description: Whether a flight in a hazard from `enter` to `leave` is there while it is valid: "before" it starts, "after" it ends, else "during", its window widened by `margin_min` either way (30, PASS_MARGIN_MIN, where missing: an ETA is an estimate); null where it gives no window.

gonogo_icing.description: Icing possible at an altitude flown, under IFR: the highest altitude at or above the freezing level, with its line; null where the flight is not planned into it.

icing_possible.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

freezing_level_at_or_below.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

reports.description: Pilot reports of icing near the route, NEG not counted.

at_or_below.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

gonogo_pass_minutes.description: Minutes after departure the flight passes a point along the route, or null.

gonogo_picked_end.description: The end the pilot picked at a field, for a takeoff or a landing, or null.

kind.description: "takeoff" or anything else for a landing.

departure.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

gonogo_risk.description: The risk assessment (PAVE, IMSAFE): its points, level, line, what to do, and every factor marked.

words.description: What to do at this level.

gonogo_risk_line.description: An assessment in a few words: "Raised · 8 points".

gonogo_runway_checks.description: The runway check at each field taken off from or landed at, fields and runways by index: the runway, pressure and density altitude, wind along and across it, and the POH's distances against its length (14 CFR 91.103(b)). Empty without both tables.

metars.description: The briefing's METARs by field ident; null or missing for none.

airports.description: The briefing's airports by field ident, each with its runways.

pressure_alt_ft.description: Null where the field's elevation is not known (see unchecked).

reported.description: A METAR gave the temperature and altimeter.

unchecked.description: Why the field's distances were not worked out (distances then empty): its elevation not known.

caveats.description: What could not be had from the table: beyond its altitudes or temperatures, heavier than its heaviest weight, a tailwind past the POH's figures, or no wind correction in the airplane's profile.

unknown.description: No runway, or its length not known: whether it fits is not known (14 CFR 91.103(b)).

beyond.description: Read past the POH's table: the figures are its edge's, not the airplane's.

gonogo_runway_flown.description: The runway and end flown: the one picked where it is there, else the one the wind favours.

gonogo_runway_in_use.description: The runway end a pilot would take off from and land on: the one most nearly into the wind (AC 90-66C 11.5), else the most used runway's first end.

gonogo_runway_number.description: A runway end's number with its leading zero dropped: "09" to "9".

gonogo_self_checks.description: The self checks the Brief's Risk page lists (IMSAFE and PAVE), in order, with no mark.

gonogo_soft_surface.description: Whether a runway's surface is grass, turf, dirt or gravel.

gonogo_sua_when.description: A special-use area's times of use read for the pass. The host works the clocks out in the area's own time zone.

utc.description: [day 0-6 (0 Sunday), minute of the day], UTC.

local.description: The same in the area's own zone; null where not known.

gonogo_tfr_when.description: A TFR's window against the pass time, widened by a margin.

gonogo_under_minimums.description: The sentences where the weather is under the pilot's own minimums, at each field landed at and the destination's forecast.

landings.description: The fields landed at, by ident.

metars.description: The briefing's METARs by field ident; null or missing for none.

airports.description: The briefing's airports by field ident, each with its runways.

forecast.description: The briefing's forecast along the route.

gonogo_verdict_items.description: Each tab's finding, in the order a pilot goes through them (AIM 7-1-5(b)), each with where it is shown in full.

gonogo_verdict_line.description: What the findings come to, in a line over them: the worst finding and the tabs that have it.

gonogo_with_alternate.description: The items with the alternate's finding put in the weather's, where the weather says nothing worse.

groundspeed_kt.description: The nav log's ground speed once the heading holds the course: the airspeed's share along it less the wind's.

handbook_figures.description: A handbook specifications page's figures, read from the text off its photo; a figure not found is left out.

handbook_read_check.description: A handbook's performance and weight and balance figures as read off a photographed page (POH sections 5 and 6), put in the app's units (knots, feet, pounds, inches, gallons) and checked, as items for the pilot to confirm: each against the band light airplanes' handbooks give (14 CFR 1.1's small airplane, 12,500 lb), and against the others (more power, more speed and burn; the distance over 50 ft no shorter than the ground roll; thinner air, longer distances, FAA-H-8083-25C chapter 11; weight times arm the moment; the CG envelope closed, at least three corners, sides not crossing; usable fuel no more than the total). Asked again with only the confirmed items, its handbook and profile are what is saved.

speed_unit.description: The speeds' unit as printed; knots where none.

cruise_speed_kind.description: What the cruise table's speeds are: true, indicated or calibrated; true where none.

distance_unit.description: The takeoff and landing distances' unit.

fuel_unit.description: The fuel quantities' unit (US gallons or litres).

burn_unit.description: The fuel burns' unit; pounds an hour are taken as avgas, 6 lb a gallon.

speed.description: Best rate of climb speed, Vy, indicated, in speed_unit.
Best glide speed, indicated, in speed_unit.

ratio.description: Feet forward for each foot down.

moment_divisor.description: What the printed moment is divided by (1,000 for "moment/1000"); 1 where none.

envelope.description: The CG envelope's corners, going round.

path.description: Where it is in the read: "cruise.2.tas".

handbook.title: HandbookFigures
handbook.description: Every figure in the app's units, for the airplane's record.

profile.title: HandbookProfile

cruise_from.description: The cruise item the cruise figures come from.

profile.description: The airplane form's figures: the cruise row at the cruise reference altitude (6,000 ft, within 1,000 ft) and the power nearest 65%, free of wrong flags.

handbook_within.description: Whether an airplane's figure, typed in or read off its handbook's page, is within the bounds a light airplane's is believed within; outside them it is a misreading.

highest_under_clouds_ft.description: The highest altitude that keeps 14 CFR 91.155(a)'s distance below a cloud base (MSL): 500 ft under it, 1,000 ft at or above 10,000 ft MSL.

hold_entry.description: The entry into a route's hold for an airplane arriving on a course (AIM 5-3-8 j.3's sectors, read by the course flown).

arrival_deg.description: The magnetic course flown to the fix.

hold_figures.description: A hold's lap and time held, in minutes, and its standard-rate turn radius (AIM 5-3-8); held_min is one lap where neither turns nor minutes is given.

hold_length_read.description: A hold's length from its code ("2T", "10M"), or null.

hold_length_write.description: A hold's length as its code, from exactly one of whole turns or minutes.

hold_read.description: A hold read from the route's text ("VPBNG/090/30:270:R:1M:2T"), or null.

hold_write.description: A hold as the route's text writes it.

holding.description: The planner's /api/holding answer (AIM 5-3-8): the entry and its steps, the other entry near a sector's edge, and the legs in the wind where a true airspeed, wind and altitude are all given.

heading.description: The airplane's heading to the fix, degrees.

altitude_ft.description: MSL; none is taken as at or below 14,000 ft.

holding_leg_minutes.description: The inbound leg's minutes (AIM 5-3-8 j.4(a)): 1 at or below 14,000 ft MSL, 1.5 above.

holds_read.description: Each comma-separated piece of text, trimmed, the empty left out, with its hold or null.

icing_forecast_route.description: Forecast icing on an IFR route (#216; AIM 7-1-4, 7-1-19): from the AWC's icing cross-section along each leg (its GFA's, from CIP and FIP), the worst severity at the altitude flown (the levels either side of it), the share of the leg in icing there, the layer icing is forecast in, the worst on the route and the Go / No-Go's line; a leg with no section is unchecked.

levels_ft.description: The sections' levels, ft MSL, climbing.

values.description: The AWC's severity, 0 none to 4 heavy, negative none forecast, level-fastest.

sfc_hgt.description: The ground under each column, m.

section.description: The AWC's cross-section along the leg, null where it could not be had.

ifr_alternate_check.description: Whether a field will do as the IFR alternate at its ETA (14 CFR 91.169(c)): the standard minimums 600 ft and 2 sm with a precision approach (ILS, GLS, PAR; (c)(1)(i)(A)), 800 and 2 without ((B)); `good` null where the pilot has to look (its own minimums, no approach, no TAF at the ETA, a ceiling of unknown height, no visibility).

ifr_alternate_destination.description: Whether the destination needs an IFR alternate (14 CFR 91.169(b)): no instrument approach, or a forecast that does not indicate at least 2,000 ft and 3 sm for an hour either side of the ETA (TEMPO and PROB included; a TAF not covering the whole window, a ceiling of unknown height or no visibility does not); no TAF needs one.

ifr_alternate_window.description: The window, unix seconds, a field's TAF is read over for 14 CFR 91.169: the destination's from an hour before to an hour after the ETA (91.169(b)(2)(i), aircraft other than helicopters); an alternate's the ETA there alone, at the estimated time of arrival at the alternate airport (91.169(c)).

ifr_alternates_ranked.description: The fields offered as the IFR alternate: those that will do, or that meet the standard minimums and publish their own, good first then nearest, `limit` of them.

items.description: An ifr_alternate_check answer with its distance_nm.

ifr_floors.description: Each leg's minimum IFR altitude (14 CFR 91.177(a)(2)): the highest of the ground given and the DOF obstacles within 4 nm of its course, plus 1,000 ft, or 2,000 ft over a mountainous area (Part 95 subpart B), rounded up to the next 100 ft.

ifr_obstacle_radius_nm.description: How far from the course 14 CFR 91.177(a)(2) takes the highest obstacle: 4 nm.

in_emergency.description: Whether an airplane is in an emergency: 7500, 7600 or 7700 set, or an emergency sent (AIM 6-2-2, 6-3-4, 6-4-2).

in_flight.description: A flight under way against its route (#218): miles along and off the course line and which side, the desired track at the airplane against its track (true, and magnetic by the World Magnetic Model where now_s is given), the fuel the nav log's legs burn to here, and the next waypoint (direct) and the destination (direct to the next, then along the route) with their miles, bearing, time at the groundspeed now, arrival and the fuel the plan leaves from fuel_start_gal. on_route within 3 nm of the line at flying speed. Null with no line. A planning aid beside the airplane's instruments (AC 120-76D).

inspections_due.description: The airplane's inspections' last good days, in calendar months (to the last day of the Nth month after the one it was done in): the annual (14 CFR 91.409(a)) and the ELT's (91.207(d)), 12; the static system and altimeter (91.411(a)) and the transponder (91.413(a)), 24; the 100-hour 100 hours of time in service on (91.409(b)); a VOR check for IFR good 30 days (91.171(a)(2)) within 4 degrees (a test signal, a surface checkpoint, one system against the other) or 6 (an airborne checkpoint, an airway radial; 91.171(b), (c)). Null where it was not given.

is_eastbound.description: Whether a magnetic course is eastbound, 0 to 179 degrees (14 CFR 91.159(a)).

isa_temp_c.description: A standard day's temperature at a pressure altitude (ICAO Doc 7488).

kept_age.description: A kept answer's age, as the apps show it with no signal ("Fetched 42 min ago"), and whether it is past the freshness ready_to_fly holds it to: the briefing, the plan's nav log, the Go / No-Go and the weather loop for an hour (the app's choice, at AIM 7-1-28's hourly METAR), METARs and TAFs for the routine report's hour (AIM 7-1-28), the NOTAMs for an hour (14 CFR 91.103, AIM 5-1-3; the age the app's choice), and the airport cards and plates for the AIRAC cycle they came in (FAA 28 and 56 Day Product Schedule). A caution at worst: the answer is still shown.

now.description: Unix seconds, UTC: the engine has no clock.

fetched_at.description: When the network gave the kept answer, Unix seconds.

finding.description: Caution once past its freshness: the line drawn in the caution colour.

fresh_min.description: How long it is fresh, minutes; null for the kinds kept for their AIRAC cycle.

kneeboard_radio.description: A field's radio as the kneeboard lists it, [short name, MHz] in its order (the tower's before the CTAF's).

least_crosswind.description: Of a field's runways, each on the end the wind favours, the least crosswind, steady or gust, whichever is more: the runway a pilot would pick to keep the wind most nearly down it. A variable wind is all crosswind (AIM 7-1-28); calm is none. null with no wind or no runway end with a heading.

variation_deg.description: The field's magnetic variation, east positive, to turn a runway's number true where its end has no true heading.

end.description: The end it is on, null for a variable wind or calm.

crosswind_kt.description: Knots, unsigned, steady or gust whichever is more.

legal_cruising_altitudes.description: Every legal cruising altitude for a magnetic course from the floor up to the ceiling, ascending: under VFR 14 CFR 91.159(a)'s thousands plus 500 under Class A (71.33), and every 500 ft up to rule_from_ft (3,000 ft over the lowest ground); under IFR 91.179(b)'s thousands (FAA Order JO 7110.65 TBL 4-5-1) to FL410.

lighting_read.description: A field's lighting remarks read for a pilot (the Chart Supplement's, NASR APT_RMK.csv LGT_SKED and BCN_LGT_SKED): each system named, by its code in the Chart Supplement legend (Airport Lighting, Visual Glideslope Indicators) and its name in AIM 2-1 (approach lights 2-1-1, visual glideslope indicators 2-1-2, REIL 2-1-3, runway edge lights by intensity 2-1-4, in-runway lighting 2-1-5, the beacon 2-1-9, taxiway lights 2-1-10), the runways it serves as written, and how it is turned on: keying the mic on the CTAF or a frequency (AIM 2-1-8, Pilot Control of Airport Lighting), when the tower is closed, at a preset intensity a pilot turns up, on a schedule (sunset to sunrise), or on all the time; the contractions written out (JO 7340.2 and the Chart Supplement's Abbreviations). A sentence not read in full is a note, its known contractions written out and every other word kept as written, never guessed. standard_keying where a light is the pilot's and the remarks give no count of clicks of their own: AIM 2-1-8's 7 (highest), 5 (medium or lower) and 3 (lowest) within 5 seconds.

lighting.description: The field's lighting remarks as sent (LGT_SKED): "WHEN ATCT CLSD, ACTVT MALSR RWY 36; REIL RWY 18 & 27 - CTAF."

beacon.description: Its beacon's remarks as sent (BCN_LGT_SKED), whose sentence naming no light is the beacon's: "DUSK-DAWN."

code.description: The Chart Supplement legend's code (MALSR, REIL, HIRL, PAPI); null where the name says it all (taxiway lights, the rotating beacon).

name.description: Its name in words: Approach lights, Runway end identifier lights, Runway edge lights, high intensity, Precision approach path indicator, Taxiway lights, Rotating beacon.

runways.description: The runways ("09/27") or runway ends ("36") it serves, as written.

pilot_controlled.description: Turned on, or up, by keying the mic (AIM 2-1-8).

frequency.description: What it is keyed on: CTAF, or a frequency as written ("122.8"); null where the remarks do not say.

clicks.description: A count of clicks the remarks give of their own.

tower_closed.description: Said of it when the tower is closed (WHEN ATCT CLSD).

preset.description: The intensity it is preset at.

brighter.description: A preset light the pilot turns up by keying (TO INCR INTST).

schedule.description: When, in words: "sunset to sunrise", "dusk to 0230", "after 0000", times as written.

continuous.description: On all the time (OPR CONSLY, H24).

nonstandard.description: NSTD: the legend's 'light system fails to meet FAA standards'.

how.description: How it is turned on in a pilot's words: "Key the mic on CTAF when the tower is closed", "Preset low, sunset to sunrise; key the mic on CTAF for more", "On all the time"; null where the remarks say none.

as_written.description: The sentence of the remark it was read from, as sent.

words.description: The sentence, its contractions written out, every other word kept.

notes.description: The sentences not read as systems, in the remarks' order.

standard_keying.description: A light is the pilot's and the remarks give no count of clicks: AIM 2-1-8's 7, 5 and 3 apply.

logbook_csv_read.description: A logbook CSV (ForeFlight's export or this logbook's own) read into the gateway's LogbookEntryRequest entries, camelCase, and the lines skipped with why; landings as 14 CFR 61.57(a) and (b) count them. Air time (not a 61.51(b) column) is this logbook's AirTime, else ForeFlight's TimeOff to TimeOn, else 0 (not known); an entry read from a file is never from a track.

airHours.description: Takeoff roll to landing roll, to the tenth, at most the flight time; 0 where the file gives none.

touchAndGoes.description: Of the day landings, those not to a full stop (61.57(a) counts them, (b) does not).

fromTrack.description: Always false: read from a file.

flightId.description: Always null: a file opens no saved flight.

logbook_csv_write.description: The logbook as a CSV file in ForeFlight's column names, oldest flight first.

logbook_from_track.description: A logbook entry drawn from the app's own flown track, a draft for the pilot to change and confirm: 14 CFR 1.1's flight time and night, 61.57's landings (full stop or touch-and-go, 61.57(b)'s period), the approaches matched to the CIFP procedures given and the holds (61.57(c), offered apart in `instrument`: they count only when flown by instruments, 61.51(g)(1)), cross-country by 61.1(b), and a reason for each figure.

points.description: The track, in any order; put in time order first.

fields.description: The fields near the places logbook_track_places named.

drawings.description: Those fields' approaches, as /api/procedure draws them.

picked.description: The approach picked for the flight, by its CIFP id.

utc_offset_min.description: The pilot's clock against UTC, minutes; 0 where left out.

airHours.description: Takeoff roll to landing roll, to the tenth.

nightHours.description: Of the flight time, in 1.1's night.

crossCountryHours.description: The flight time where a landing was more than 50 nm from the departure (61.1(b)(ii)), else 0.

dayLandings.description: Every landing not counted at night: 61.57(a).

nightLandings.description: To a full stop in 61.57(b)'s period.

touchAndGoes.description: Of the day landings, the touch-and-goes (61.57(a) counts them, (b) does not).

approaches.description: 0: added from `instrument` where flown by instruments.

instrument.title: LogbookInstrument
instrument.description: 61.57(c)(1)'s items the track shows, to add to the entry where flown by instruments.

faf_at.description: When it crossed the final approach fix inbound, ms.

logbook_read_check.description: A paper logbook page as read off a photograph, each row a draft of the gateway's logbook entry with what to check (14 CFR 61.51(b): the date, total time, where from and to, the airplane; each kind of time no longer than the flight; dual and solo not overlapping, 61.51(d); approaches and holds with instrument time, 61.51(g)(1), 61.57(c); night landings with night time, 61.57(b); cross-country with a landing elsewhere, 61.1), and the page's own totals against its rows.

night_landings.description: Night landings to a full stop.

page_totals.title: LogbookPageTotals
page_totals.description: The page's "total this page" row, where it has one.

today.description: The caller's date, YYYY-MM-DD: a row dated after it is wrong.

entry.title: LogbookEntryDraft

flownOn.description: YYYY-MM-DD; null where no date was read.

entry.description: The gateway's LogbookEntryRequest, as the page gives it.

flags.description: The page's: its totals against its rows.

logbook_track_places.description: Where a flown track took off, landed or came down low, for the host to find the fields within `within_nm` of each (the logbook entry drawn from the track, pilot's autolog).

points.description: The track, in any order; put in time order first.

within_nm.description: How far round each place a field is looked for.

lost_comms.description: The planner's /api/lost-comms answer (14 CFR 91.185): VFR's words, the routes in the rule's order (c)(1), each segment's altitude (c)(2) and when to leave the clearance limit (c)(3).

expected_from.description: The index of the segment from which the expected altitude applies, a whole number; 0 where left out.

lowest_vfr_cruising_altitude.description: The lowest VFR cruising altitude at or above a floor for a magnetic course: odd thousands plus 500 eastbound, even westbound (14 CFR 91.159(a)).

magnetic_variation.description: Magnetic variation, degrees east (west negative), the World Magnetic Model's (WMM) at a place and day, as wingtip.magnetic works it out.

year.description: The model's decimal year (2026.5 mid-2026), in place of the date.

mayday_call.description: The distress call in AIM 6-3-2(a)(3)'s order, filled from what the app knows, each part it does not know a blank in brackets and listed in missing; the code (7700, AIM 6-2-2; an assigned code kept while talking to ATC, 6-3-2(a)(2)); and the frequencies to call on: the one in use, the nearest approach or departure control and tower the app lists, then 121.5 MHz.

position.description: As a controller gives it: "BAE 245° 12 nm".

mode_c_veil.description: The nearest Mode C veil airport (14 CFR part 91 appendix D section 1) within 30 nm of a point (91.215(b)(2), 91.225(d)(2)), the distance to a tenth; null outside every veil. An airport with no place is passed over.

morse.description: A navaid's ident in Morse code (AIM 1-1-3), the letters two spaces apart.

n_number.description: Whether text is a US registration, an N-number (14 CFR 47.15(b)).

navaid_hours.description: A navaid's hours as filed ("24" is "Continuous"), or null where none are filed.

navlog_alternate_leg.description: The leg from the destination on to the IFR alternate for 14 CFR 91.167(a)(2)'s fuel, at the last altitude in its air, or in still air (still_air) where none was read or the leg cannot be flown in it.

profile.description: null is no airplane picked: the legs' courses, miles, altitudes and air, and every figure that needs an airplane null (the owner, 2026-11-09: "don't assume").

navlog_approach_end.description: Where a flight landing by an instrument approach comes down to: the first fix not of the missed approach with an altitude under the cruise -- the chart's lowest for it, else its highest (CIFP, ARINC 424-18 5.29; AIM 5-4-5) -- and that fix's distance from the field, as navlog_with_descents takes them. Null where no fix is under the cruise: down to the pattern.

navlog_candidates.description: The altitudes each leg's plans may fly, held under 12,500 ft (14 CFR 91.211) where a leg has a choice and the airplane carries no oxygen: the ones the planner looks the air up at. Null where a leg has none.

profile.description: null is no airplane picked: the legs' courses, miles, altitudes and air, and every figure that needs an airplane null (the owner, 2026-11-09: "don't assume").

navlog_fuel_plan.description: The fuel required: the airplane's own start, taxi and takeoff allowance (its profile's taxi_fuel_gal; taxi_gal null and left out of the fuel required where its profile has none, never a stock airplane's), the trip, the IFR alternate (14 CFR 91.167(a)(2)) and the reserve, 30 min by day and 45 at night under VFR (91.151(a)), and 45 where `night` is null (no departure time: night cannot be ruled out, so the larger is assumed), 45 under IFR (91.167(a)(3)); and the margin against the usable fuel.

profile.description: null is no airplane picked: the legs' courses, miles, altitudes and air, and every figure that needs an airplane null (the owner, 2026-11-09: "don't assume").

night.description: Whether the flight is at night (14 CFR 1.1, after the end of evening civil twilight); null where it has no departure time, which takes the night's 45-minute VFR reserve (91.151(a)(2)).

navlog_fuel_stop_need.description: What a flight's fuel stops are looked for by (route options' fuel_stops): null where its fuel check passes or a figure it needs is not known (no airplane, an unflyable leg); else the worst burn a mile over a tankful's stretch of its legs and its minutes a mile, each times the route's miles for each straight one, the usable fuel, the start and taxi allowance, and the reserve -- 14 CFR 91.151(a)(2)'s 45 minutes for (a)(1)'s 30 where any of a VFR trip, its stops' turnarounds counted, is at night; 91.167(a)(3)'s under IFR as given.

totals.description: The flight's nav log totals with its fuel check (navlog_totals, navlog_fuel_plan).

depart_s.description: The departure, unix seconds (now where none was given: the engine has no clock).

navlog_hold.description: The leg with a pilot's hold flown on it (AIM 5-3-8): its minutes at the leg's TAS and cruise burn added to the leg's time and fuel, and the hold's entry from the course flown to the fix (j.3) and its no-wind racetrack in true degrees.

navlog_join_figures.description: A route with stops' figures at each altitude any hop offers, each hop at its own nearest; times and fuel unknown and none flown everywhere where a hop offers none.

navlog_join_plans.description: A route with stops' four plans from each hop's: steps in turn, times and fuel summed (null where a hop's is), the tailwind weighed by each hop's length; none where a hop has none.

navlog_leg.description: One leg from start to end at an altitude in the air given (wingtip.navlog.assemble_leg): true course and distance, the airplane's cruise in its air, the wind triangle (PHAK ch. 16), magnetic heading (true less variation, east positive), ground speed, time and fuel; an unflyable leg's time is null.

profile.description: null is no airplane picked: the legs' courses, miles, altitudes and air, and every figure that needs an airplane null (the owner, 2026-11-09: "don't assume").

navlog_legs.description: A leg between each consecutive pair of fixes, all at altitude_ft, each in its own air (air, one a leg).

profile.description: null is no airplane picked: the legs' courses, miles, altitudes and air, and every figure that needs an airplane null (the owner, 2026-11-09: "don't assume").

navlog_legs_at.description: The legs flown at the altitude target_ft picked on the wheel: each leg at it where legal, else at its nearest legal altitude (the lower on a tie), with their climbs.

profile.description: null is no airplane picked: the legs' courses, miles, altitudes and air, and every figure that needs an airplane null (the owner, 2026-11-09: "don't assume").

navlog_plans.description: The four altitude plans -- lowest and highest over the legal band, fastest by the winds, economical by the fuel, each paying its climbs -- and the route flown at each legal altitude (by_altitude). Empty where a leg has no legal altitude.

profile.description: null is no airplane picked: the legs' courses, miles, altitudes and air, and every figure that needs an airplane null (the owner, 2026-11-09: "don't assume").

navlog_totals.description: The legs' totals: miles (procedures' miles more included), time and fuel (null while a leg is unflyable), unflyable legs and legs with no winds aloft.

navlog_with_climbs.description: The legs with their climbs flown, from the field (start_altitude_ft; null starts level) and at every step up, at the best rate in each leg's air and the climb speed; each leg's climb_min and the top of climb (toc).

profile.description: null is no airplane picked: the legs' courses, miles, altitudes and air, and every figure that needs an airplane null (the owner, 2026-11-09: "don't assume").

navlog_with_descents.description: The legs with their tops of descent at three to one (333 ft a nm, about a 3 degree path, AIM 2-1-2's VASI glide path) to the pattern altitude where the 45-degree entry begins, about 1.7 nm before the end (AC 90-66C 11.2, 11.3: level at pattern altitude before entering), to an approach's fix end_before_nm short of it, and to a lower leg's altitude by the fix it starts at -- or, for a leg marked start_at (a pilot's Start At), from that fix on, the top of descent at the end of the leg before; the times and fuel unchanged.

end_before_nm.description: How far before the legs' end the descent is finished, nm: an approach's fix's distance out; where not given, down to a pattern, where the 45-degree entry begins (limits::pattern_entry_start_nm, about 1.7 nm), and 0 with an end_fix.

night_at_either_end.description: Whether a flight is at night leaving `start` at `depart_s` or arriving at `end` at `arrive_s` (14 CFR 1.1; 91.151(a)'s reserve).

night_on_the_way.description: Whether any of a trip from `start` to `end` of `minutes` (its stops' time on the ground counted), leaving at `depart_s`, falls in the night, judged every half hour along the straight line: 14 CFR 91.151(a)(2)'s 45 minutes then.

no_altitude.description: Why no plan has an altitude, in a pilot's words: where it fails, the reasons there, what to do, whether Class B is what stops it, and all of it as one message.

notam_read.description: A NOTAM read for a pilot, beside its text as sent: its keyword (FAA Order JO 7930.2 1-2-1) as a plain heading, or the ICAO Q) code's subject (Appendix B); its words with the FAA's contractions written out (JO 7340.2; JO 7930.2 3-3-1 and TBL 3-3-1) in sentence case, its codes (ILS, PAPI, VOR, RNAV, LPV) and idents kept, runways and taxiways as designated (3-3-5, 3-3-6), heights MSL unless AGL is stated (4-2-1), distances and compass points from a place, coordinates and fix-radial-distances written out; and its start of activity and end of validity in UTC (YYMMDDHHMM, 3-3-2), with EST (an estimate) and PERM (permanent) (4-2-1). Its what, where and why in our words where its subject's words say them (the airport card's four lines). A word it does not know is kept as written, never guessed.

text.description: The NOTAM as sent: the domestic form ("!OSH 11/041 OSH RWY 18/36 CLSD 2511120900-2511121700") or the ICAO form (Q) A) B) C) E) ...).

idents.description: The field's idents (OSH, KOSH), kept as written in its words.

form.description: The form it was read in; text where it is in neither, its words then as sent.

keyword.description: Its JO 7930.2 keyword (RWY, TWY, AD, OBST, NAV, IAP ...).

heading.description: What it is about, in words: Runway, Taxiway, Obstacle, Instrument approach, Temporary flight restriction ...

title.description: The thing it is about, named by the words straight after its keyword (1-2-1), as notam_subject reads them: a runway or taxiway as designated (3-3-5, 3-3-6: "Runway 06/24", "Taxiways B and C"), an apron, an ILS's part by its runway ("Glide slope runway 09"), a navaid by its ident ("OSH VOR"), an FDC approach NOTAM's procedure as the plate prints it (7-1-3), an obstacle's kind ("Obstacle: crane"), the fuel and its grade ("Fuel 100LL"), a facility and its frequency ("Tower 120.75"), the field's beacon or closure. Null where they name nothing it knows: the heading is then the title.

what.description: In our words, one line: what it is and its condition ("Runway 04L/22R closed except taxiing", "Glide slope runway 09 out of service", "Crane 759 ft MSL (145 ft above ground)", "ILS Z RWY 10R (SA CAT I): not authorized"), said only where its subject's words (1-2-1) say all of it; null otherwise, its words then standing in.

where.description: The field and the place on it as the NOTAM gives it: "KORD, runway 06/24", "KORD, taxiway A2 between taxiway A and taxiway B", "KORD, 1.3 nm west of the field"; null where it says no more than the field.

why.description: What it means to the pilot, only where that is a settled rule or a plain fact: a runway or the field closed, no landing or takeoff (CLSD, JO 7340.2), crossing or taxiing where EXC XNG or EXC TAX allows it; the glide slope out, a localizer approach to the LOC minimums, the localizer or the ILS out, no ILS or localizer approach (AIM 1-1-9); a PAPI or VASI out, no visual glide path guidance (AIM 2-1-2); approach lights out, visibility minimums may be higher (AIM 2-1-1, 1-1-9); an FDC approach NOTAM's minimums in place of the chart's (AIM 5-1-3) or the procedure not authorized; fuel not available; a frequency out of service; an obstacle's top; a TFR's limits to read (14 CFR 91.137-91.145, 91.103). Null otherwise, never guessed.

words.description: Its words written out in sentence case, ending as a sentence ends.

starts.description: Its start of activity, ISO 8601 UTC, from its text.

ends.description: Its end of validity, ISO 8601 UTC; null where it is permanent or not given.

estimated.description: The end is an estimate (EST): it may end sooner.

permanent.description: PERM: the condition is permanent, until published.

notam_subject.description: What one NOTAM addresses on an airport's card, from its text as sent (FAA Order JO 7930.2, the domestic form of 4-2-1 and the ICAO form of chapter 8), matched to the card's own rows: the field (AD AP CLSD), a runway by its designation (RWY, 1-2-1 and 3-3-5; never a runway a taxiway's NOTAM names, 3-3-6), a light on it (PAPI, VASI, REIL, the approach lights, the edge lights, the beacon; AIM 2-1), the approaches an ILS, LOC, LDA or SDF serves (NAV) or the procedure an FDC IAP NOTAM titles (7-1-3), a frequency by its MHz or its facility (COM), the fuel (SVC), and a TFR near the field. Each with its badge's word (Closed, Closed at times, Part closed, Restricted, Out of service, Not available, Not authorized (NA, JO 7340.2), Changed, NOTAM, TFR) and how bad (unusable: closed, or a procedure not authorized; caution: the rest). CLSD EXC XNG or EXC TAX is still closed to landing and takeoff, said in the label. A NOTAM it cannot place answers no badge, never a guess.

text.description: The NOTAM as sent, domestic or ICAO form.

tfr.description: The planner's kind "tfr": a TFR within 5 nm of the field.

idents.description: The field's idents (DLH, KDLH), kept as written in the label.

runways.description: The card's runways as it names them ("09/27", "18L/36R"), in its order.

lights.description: The card's lights as lighting_read names them, in its order.

approaches.description: The card's approach charts by their titles ("ILS OR LOC RWY 09"), in its order.

frequencies.description: The card's frequencies, their type (TWR, ATIS, AWOS) and MHz, in its order.

on.description: What the badge goes next to.

index.description: Its row in the list the card gave (runways, lights, approaches, frequencies); null for the field and the fuel.

word.description: The badge's word, in sentence case.

label.description: What it says, for the badge's label: the NOTAM's words (notam_read), or what a closure leaves open.

notams_fns.description: The NOTAMs of one FAA NOTAM System (FNS) message, AIXM 5.1, as wingtip.notams keeps them: each by its domestic place and number, else its place and ICAO number; `ends` the sooner of its own end and its feature lifetime's. None where the message is not XML.
