notams_ranked.description: A flight's NOTAMs ranked by what bears on it (14 CFR 91.103: all available information concerning the flight): in force while it is at the field or en route, at its departure, stops or destination, naming the runway in use, closing the field, an altitude span (FAA JO 7930.2 chapter 5; the ICAO Q) line's limits) taking in the cruise altitude, an airspace the route passes. The top three in force are said first; none is dropped.

location.description: The place the NOTAM is issued for, as the feed names it (OSH, KOSH).

starts.description: ISO 8601 UTC; null for in force now.

ends.description: ISO 8601 UTC; null for until further notice.

floor_ft.description: A TFR's floor, ft MSL, where the planner read it.

crosses.description: The route goes through it (a TFR the planner placed on the route).

from.description: When the flight's time at the field starts, ISO 8601 UTC.

runways.description: The runway ends in use there ("18", "09L"); empty where none is known.

from.description: The flight's window, ISO 8601 UTC: for a NOTAM at no field of the route.

airspaces.description: The airspaces the route passes, by name (CHICAGO CLASS B).

top.description: One of the first three said with a line each; the rest are folded.

tied.description: Another NOTAM has the same score: the words may put a tie in another order.

keyword.description: Its JO 7930.2 keyword (RWY, AD, NAV, AIRSPACE...).

our_call.description: Whether a transmission is said to the airplane `tail` (AIM 4-2-4).

own_altitude_caution.description: What an altitude the pilot set for a hop breaks against the band the planner worked out for each leg, as warnings: under the floor (14 CFR 91.119), off 91.159(a)'s altitudes, into Class B (91.131), over the service ceiling, inside 91.155's cloud clearance, in Class A (71.33(a), 91.135), past 91.211(a)'s oxygen heights; under IFR the minimum IFR altitude (91.177(a)) and 91.179(b)'s thousands. Null where nothing is.

profile.description: The airplane: `supplemental_oxygen` or `pressurized` true takes 91.211's cautions away.

own_ship_hex.description: Which airplane heard is own ship's own transponder: its hex, or null.

passenger_briefing.description: The passengers' briefing in the order of the FAA's SAFETY briefing (FAA Safety Briefing, Jan/Feb 2007 and Jul/Aug 2014): 14 CFR 91.107(a)(1)'s belts and (a)(2), (3)'s fastened for taxi, takeoff and landing, the rest the Private Pilot ACS's PA.II.B.S2 guidance, each with where it comes from.

passenger_night.description: Whether an instant is in 14 CFR 61.57(b)'s night-passenger period at a point: from 1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise (the sun's centre 0.833 degrees down, NOAA's solar calculation), its own window rather than 14 CFR 1.1's night, so a high-latitude summer night with no 1.1 night still has it.

passenger_night_on_the_way.description: Whether any of a flight from `start` to `end` of `minutes`, leaving at `depart_s`, falls in 14 CFR 61.57(b)'s night-passenger period, judged every half hour along the straight line as night_on_the_way judges the night.

pattern_altitude.description: A field's traffic pattern altitude: the published height, else 1,000 ft above the field (AC 90-66C).

altitude_ft.description: Feet MSL, whole; null with no elevation.

flown_ft.description: Feet MSL to the nearest hundred (halves to even), as the planner flies down to it; null with no elevation.

pattern_entry.description: How to join the pattern for an end, coming on a course (AC 90-66C 11.3).

traffic.description: "right" for right traffic; anything else, or none, is left (14 CFR 91.126(b)(1)).

pattern_side.description: Whether it comes from the pattern's side.

traffic.description: "right" for right traffic; anything else, or none, is left (14 CFR 91.126(b)(1)).

pattern_side.description: The bearing, degrees true, from the runway to its pattern's side: right traffic to the right, else left (14 CFR 91.126(b)(1)).

traffic.description: "right" for right traffic; anything else, or none, is left (14 CFR 91.126(b)(1)).

performance_climb.description: A best-rate climb's minutes and gallons, its rate falling with density altitude to 100 fpm at the service ceiling (PHAK ch. 11), in air isa_dev_c warmer than a standard day; nothing for a descent.

performance_cruise.description: An airplane's cruise at an altitude in air at oat_c (a standard day's where null): its power at the cruise setting or full throttle (Gagg and Ferrar), TAS as the cube root of power over density, burn with power, and the density altitude.

pilot_currency.description: Where the pilot stands on a day, from the logbook and the dates they give: passengers by day (14 CFR 61.57(a)) and at night (61.57(b)), the flight review (61.56(c)), the medical, the logbook's totals and instrument currency (61.57(c)(1), (d)). The gateway's CurrencyDto.

medical_expires_on.description: The day the medical expires, as the pilot gives it, YYYY-MM-DD.

ipc_on.description: The last instrument proficiency check (61.57(d)), YYYY-MM-DD.

dayPassengersUntil.description: 90 days after the third most recent landing (61.57(a)); null with fewer than three.

nightPassengersUntil.description: 90 days after the third most recent night full-stop landing (61.57(b)).

flightReviewOn.description: YYYY-MM-DD; null where none can be had.

flightReviewUntil.description: The end of the 24th calendar month after the flight review's (61.56(c)).

medicalExpiresOn.description: YYYY-MM-DD; null where none can be had.

totalHours.description: Every entry's hours, to the tenth.

instrumentCurrentUntil.description: The last day of instrument currency (61.57(c)(1), or 61.57(d)'s check); in the past where it has lapsed, null where none is logged.

instrumentCurrentFrom.description: The first day of an instrument currency not begun yet: approaches, holding and tracking flown this month count from the first of next month (61.57(c)(1), 'the 6 calendar months preceding the month of the flight'), so until then the pilot is not current and instrumentCurrentUntil is the end of the currency to come. Null when current now, lapsed or none logged.

ipcOn.description: YYYY-MM-DD; null where none can be had.

ipcNeededAfter.description: The day after which only an instrument proficiency check restores it: six calendar months past instrumentCurrentUntil (61.57(d)).

approachesInWindow.description: Approaches logged in the 6 calendar months before this one (61.57(c)(1)(i)).

trackingInWindow.description: Intercepting and tracking courses logged in them (61.57(c)(1)(iii)).

pilot_experience.description: A student's aeronautical experience for a private pilot certificate, airplane single-engine (14 CFR 61.109(a)), item by item as the logbook shows it on the day. The gateway's ExperienceItemDto each.

pirep_conditions.description: A PIREP's turbulence and icing in words, or null where it reports neither.

pireps_along_route.description: The PIREPs of the last 90 minutes at or under 18,000 ft within the corridor of the route, urgent first, then in route order, each with along_track_nm.

pireps_in_box.description: The PIREPs still told (the last 90 minutes, at or under 18,000 ft) in a box, the urgent last.

place_name.description: A town's name as it is spelt ("McCook"), from text, or each of texts as a list (a null row answers "").

place_words.description: Words for a place as the planner looks them up, the ICAO alphabet's spelled (AIM 4-2-7).

plan_profile.description: The plan's altitudes along the route, from the nav log's rows: climbs, levels, descents at three to one.

planning_figures.description: The planner's own planning figures, one copy for the apps: the time on the ground at a stop the pilot gave none for, a 30-minute turnaround (the owner's pick, 2026-10-20), and the altitude an airplane's cruise TAS and fuel burn are taken as its own at on a standard day, 6,000 ft (a row of every handbook's cruise table, FAA-H-8083-25C ch. 11).

point_kind.description: What a route point typed is: a fix, the pilot's own point (fix-radial-distance), or null.

pressure_altitude_ft.description: Pressure altitude from a field's elevation and its altimeter setting: the standard atmosphere's height of the setting above 29.92 "Hg, (1 - (setting/29.92)^(1/5.2558797)) x 145,442 ft (ICAO Doc 7488), FAA-H-8083-25C ch. 11 Figure 11-3's conversion factor to within 2 ft (30.10 "Hg: -165).

procedure_arc.description: An RF leg's arc round its centre fix, or an AF (DME arc) leg's round its navaid (ARINC 424 5.21): points from start to end, turning right (clockwise) or left, one every five degrees, at the centre's distance from the end.

procedure_climb_nm.description: How far a leg flown to an altitude (CA, VA, FA) is drawn, nm: from the altitude known at its start at 200 ft a nm (FAA Order 8260.3), within 1 to 15; 2 nm where either is not known or it is no climb.

procedure_hold.description: A CIFP hold's racetrack (HA, HF, HM) at its fix, inbound on the true course to the fix, turning right or left, with standard-rate turns at a light airplane's 120 kt (AIM 5-3-8): the fix, the turn out, the outbound leg, the turn in, and back to the fix.

procedure_hold_leg_nm.description: A hold's leg, nm: a timed leg flown at 120 kt (AIM 5-3-8 j.4), else the distance the CIFP codes; null with neither.

procedure_turn.description: A 45°/180° procedure turn at its fix (AIM 5-4-9): 4 nm out on the final's reciprocal, 2 nm on the barb's true course, a standard-rate 180° turn at 120 kt toward the final's side, back to meet the final within 10 nm, and in to the fix.

procedures_read.description: Each piece of the route's procedures text with its pick as the web app reads it, or null, and whether it is one exactly as the planner takes it.

procedures_write.description: The route's procedures text from the picks (an empty transition or direct is none).

proficiency_plan.description: A pilot's proficiency plan: what is due and when (the flight review, 14 CFR 61.56(c); passengers by day and at night, 61.57(a), (b); instrument currency, 61.57(c), (d); a student's solo endorsement, 61.87(n), (p); the medical as given), the reminders for those lapsing within remind_days, the weak areas the pilot's own debriefs show (an approach off course or glidepath under the 500 ft gate, AC 61-98D 2.1.4; an approach past full scale or under a minimum; a downwind off pattern altitude, ACS PA.III.B; a leg not held, PA.VI.A), each with its evidence, and up to four sessions: what to practise, why, the nearest suited field of `places`, how long, and whether it may count toward a WINGS flight activity (AC 61-91K 7.3). Every decision is the engine's; a model only words it, citing the ids.

medical_expires_on.description: YYYY-MM-DD, as the pilot gives it.

ipc_on.description: The last instrument proficiency check, YYYY-MM-DD.

ratings.description: "student" holds the pilot to the solo endorsement instead of the flight review (61.56(g)); "instrument" adds instrument currency.

remind_days.description: How many days before a currency lapses its reminder shows; 30 where null.

reminders.description: The currencies lapsing within remind_days, in a sentence each.

procedure.description: The approach procedure flown ("ILS Y RWY 08"), where the line is an approach's.

evidence.description: The lines from the pilot's debriefs of the last half year.

profile_clearance.description: The profile's clearance preview at an altitude: the ground samples and obstacles along the route coloured red where they come within less than 500 ft of it or above it (14 CFR 91.119(c)'s 500 ft above the surface and from any structure; exactly 500 ft meets it) and yellow within 1,000 ft (91.119(b)'s height over a congested area, the town not known here) -- the legal floors themselves are 91.119 (VFR) and 91.177 (IFR), which the legal altitudes keep -- with the highest point, the least clearance, where the route first meets ground at or over the altitude, the route point nearest, and the whole in words for VoiceOver and TalkBack ("3,500 ft, terrain within 500 ft near KXYZ").

prohibited_caution.description: Prohibited airspace on the way as warnings (14 CFR 73.83), from the selection's `special_use`.

radial_of.description: The radial from a VOR a point is on, the course to the station and the distance, or null where the station has no magnetic variation.

radio_call_sign.description: The airplane's call sign as spoken: its make and its registration, the N dropped (AIM 4-2-4), or a blank for the registration.

radio_place_name.description: What a pilot calls a field: its name without Airport, International and the like; its ident where nothing is left.

radio_script.description: A route's radio calls, field by field (AIM 4-2, AC 90-66C): the broadcast to listen to first, the tower's or the CTAF's calls, flight following, and the arrival, figures as spoken (AIM 4-2-8, 4-2-9).

takeoff.description: The runway end the host picked (gonogo_runway_flown); null where none has a heading.

landing.description: The runway end the host picked (gonogo_runway_flown); null where none has a heading.

read_atis.description: An ATIS or AWOS/ASOS broadcast heard, read into its figures (AIM 4-1-13); a figure not heard is null.

read_clearance.description: An ATC clearance heard, read into its items as the web's lib/clearance read it (AIM 4-4-3), camelCase.

read_datis.description: A digital ATIS as the tower's data link writes it (STDDS TDES DATISData), read into read_atis's figures, its weather from its METAR groups; a figure not read is null.

read_track.description: A GPX or KML track read: its points in time order, or the words for the pilot where it has none to use.

readback_check.description: A readback against the clearance or instruction heard (AIM 4-4-7 b): what was missed or said otherwise, each marked where 4-4-7 b asks it be read back, and the warning line; with `tail`, the call sign too (4-4-7 b.1).

ready_to_fly.description: Ready to fly: whether the device holds what the flight needs before it loses the signal -- the route's charts kept and of the 56-day edition in force, the cycle packs of the AIRAC cycle in force (FAA 28 and 56 Day Product Schedule; 14 CFR 91.103), a weather briefing under an hour old (the app's choice, at AIM 7-1-28's hourly METAR), each field's METAR in force and its TAF, the route's NOTAMs under an hour old (91.103, AIM 5-1-3; the age the app's choice), the plan's route, airplane and altitude (none assumed), what Keep for the Air holds for the route (its ages are kept_age's), the plan saved, location allowed, the battery at half or charging (the app's choice) and an ADS-B receiver where the pilot uses one. A caution at worst, never a stop; one line and at most three actions, the most pressing first.

now.description: Unix seconds, UTC: the engine has no clock.

plan.description: The flight plan: a route, the airplane's name and the cruise altitude, null where not set.

can_keep.description: False where the platform cannot keep tiles (a browser with no service worker).

charts.description: The route's offline chart tiles: kept or not, the kept edition's effective date (YYYY-MM-DD) and the download's size. Null leaves the item out.

packs.description: The cycle packs (airports, airspace, procedures): the AIRAC edition held (YYYY-MM-DD), null where none is. Null leaves the item out.

fields.description: The departure, destination and alternate: each METAR's observed time (Unix seconds) and whether a TAF is in.

on_board.description: The kinds kept on the device for this route.

missing.description: The kinds the route has and the device does not yet.

size_mb.description: What Keep for the Air downloads or holds for them, megabytes.

kept.description: What Keep for the Air holds for the route beside its charts. Null leaves the item out.

device.description: What the platform tells: a member null or missing leaves its item out.

next_cycle.description: YYYY-MM-DD: the next AIRAC cycle's first day.

receiver_nexrad.description: FIS-B NEXRAD to draw (products 63 and 64, AIM 4-5-9): for each level 1 to 7, rectangles [south, west, north, east], the regional product's where sent and the CONUS product's elsewhere, with the newest block's time. Not for avoiding weather close in.

picture.description: The last answer, or null at first.

receiver_read.description: A portable ADS-B receiver's GDL 90 bytes (Garmin 560-1058-00 Rev A; ForeFlight's ID message) read into what it has said: its state, own ship, the traffic it hears (AIM 4-5-7, 4-5-8) and the FIS-B products it is sent (AIM 4-5-9), each dropped once it is no longer heard. Traffic is for seeing, not avoiding (AIM 4-5-7).

data.description: The bytes received since the last read (whole UDP datagrams), Base64 (RFC 4648).

at.description: Now, Unix s: when the bytes came.

picture.description: The last answer, or null at first.

receiver_reports.description: A field's latest METAR (or SPECI) and TAF sent over FIS-B (AIM 4-5-9), as sent, with when; the K of a contiguous-states ICAO identifier matched either way (ORD, KORD).

picture.description: The last answer, or null at first.

receiver_traffic.description: The traffic to draw: the receiver's own targets, their pressure altitudes put on own ship's scale by own ship's height less its pressure altitude, then the internet's airplanes the receiver does not hear (by ICAO address), never own ship.

picture.description: The last answer, or null at first.

own_ft.description: Own ship's height MSL from the phone's GPS, ft, where known.

region_of.description: The phone pack's region holding a point, "n40w088": a square of 4 degrees named by its south-west corner.

registered_profile.description: The stock profile an airplane the FAA's registry names flies on, or null.

remarks_read.description: An airport's remarks in words (the Chart Supplement's, NASR APT_RMK.csv): its fuel's, its FBO's and its courtesy car's, each a line. Each contraction of one meaning written out, by the Chart Supplement's General Information Abbreviations first (CUST customs, TSNT transient, avbl available, hr hour, O/R on request, thru through) and FAA Order JO 7340.2R's decode after it, to which it defers; a code (FBO, CBP, CTAF, 100LL, Jet A), a figure, a time and a telephone number kept as written; a contraction of more than one meaning (OPR, OPN, FM) and any word not known kept as written, never guessed; the rest in sentence case. A remark with any lower case is someone's own writing, as sent.

remarks.description: The remarks as sent: "CUST CLNC 2 HR PPR - 847-894-7292. TSNT UTILIZE FBO AFT CLR CUST. FBO CBP USER FEE."

lines.description: Each remark in words, in their order: "Customs clearance 2 hours prior permission required - 847-894-7292. Transient utilize FBO after clearing customs. FBO CBP user fee."

reserve_min.description: The fuel reserve in minutes at normal cruise: 30 by day and 45 at night under VFR (14 CFR 91.151(a)), 45 under IFR (91.167(a)(3)).

route_options.description: The ways to fly a route (route/options.rs): the fastest, the best weather's, the fewest stops' and the one over land, each clear of thunderstorms by 20 nm (AIM 7-1-27), weather under the pilot's minimums and never under 14 CFR 91.155's, SIGMETs and IFR G-AIRMETs, prohibited areas (91.133), TFRs (91.137-91.145) and ground the airplane cannot top with 1,000 ft (91.119), with the fuel stops that land with 91.151's reserve; the pilot's own route and the most filed one with the stops they need; what the straight line, the ends and the pilot's route meet; the hazards; the sources not checked; and the fuel fields weighed whose places to eat were not read.

route_options_frame.description: Route options' frame, before the planner reads for it: the grid's corner, cells (0.25 degrees) and samples a cell's side, the highest VFR cruising altitude the airplane reaches either way (14 CFR 91.159 under its ceiling and Class A's 18,000 ft, 71.33), the flight's time, the cruising altitudes the winds are wanted at, the lowest cruise the water's glide is judged from, whether METARs are read (a flight leaving within two hours), the grid's box and the box the fixes and fields are wanted in.

tas_kt.description: The true airspeed the ways are costed at: the airplane's cruise, else with none picked the still-air reference (100 kt), for the host's glide reach of dry land.

route_position.description: Where an airplane is along the planned route: the nearest point of `line` (or of the route's own `points`, those not placed left out), the miles along it, to go and off it, whether it is on the route (within 3 nm, the debrief's tolerance for the distance from the planned route, ACS PA.VI.A.S5), the leg it is on and how far along it (by the legs' miles where `legs` is given, else by the points, an index into `points` as given), and the fuel the plan's legs have burnt by there (planning figures, not a gauge); null with no line to be on.

runway_calm.description: Whether a runway's wind is a calm one: no head-, cross- or gust's crosswind.

runway_crosswind.description: A runway's wind's crosswind, steady or gust, whichever is more.

runway_end_fit.description: Whether an end fits the airplane today for a takeoff or a landing: crosswind against the demonstrated, distance needed against the length with SAFO 19001's 15 per cent margin.

elevation_ft.description: Null where the field's elevation is not known: no distance is worked out (needed_ft null, unknown true).

close.description: Not short, but within SAFO 19001's 15 per cent.

unknown.description: The distance or the runway's length is not known, so whether it fits is not (14 CFR 91.103(b)); never read as fitting.

beyond.description: The distance was read past the POH's table (higher, hotter, heavier or more tailwind than it goes): its edge's figures.

runway_end_heading.description: A runway end's true heading, the table's or its number's magnetic heading turned true; null where it has neither.

runway_end_key.description: A runway end's ident as a key: its number, trimmed and upper-cased.

runway_ends_traffic.description: Each end's ident, true heading and traffic (right where its key is in `right`, else left, 14 CFR 91.126(b)(1)).

right.description: Ends' keys flown with right traffic.

runway_with_winds.description: Each runway's favoured end, the planner's RunwayWind or null.

runways_read.description: Each piece of the route's runway picks ("KSTL:30R,KMSN:36") with its pick, or null.

rvr_check.description: Each runway end's lowest RVR reading against a minimum, an RVR (ft) or a visibility (SM) by 14 CFR 91.175(h)(2)'s comparable values; a minimum between rows asks the next row up, one past 1 1/4 SM is not judged.

minimum_ft.description: The minimum as an RVR, ft; null where it has none.

at_most.description: The reading is the system's most, 6,000 ft or more.

comparable_sm.description: The visibility the table pairs with the reading.

same_field.description: Whether a and b name one field (KSTL and STL).

select_cruise_altitude.description: The planner's altitude selection from the data it read: each leg's band (the floor up to the lowest of the Class B shelf, 91.155's distance under the forecast clouds and the service ceiling, none in prohibited airspace; under IFR the service ceiling and an airway's MAA alone), its legal altitudes by its own magnetic course, the route's, the lowest recommended, and icing where a legal altitude reaches the freezing level with moisture.

floors.description: vfr_floors' or ifr_floors' answer, a floor a leg.

service_ceilings_ft.description: Null on a leg: no airplane, no ceiling of its own.

service_ceiling_on_the_day.description: The service ceiling on the day: the book's service ceiling, a density altitude (where the best climb has fallen to 100 fpm, FAA-H-8083-25C ch. 11), found as an altitude in the forecast's temperatures (wingtip_flight::performance::altitude_at_density_altitude) to the nearest 100 ft; the book figure where the profile is empty.

book_ft.description: The profile's service ceiling, a standard day's.

service_volume.description: A VOR's standard service volume by NASR's ALT_CODE (AIM 1-1-8 TBL 1-1-1), or null for a code not in the table.

short_airspace_name.description: An airspace's name shortened for a card.

sigmets_along_route.description: The SIGMETs in force whose area the route crosses (FAA-H-8083-28B 26.2.4).

solo_standing.description: A student's 61.87(n) solo endorsement on the instructor's list: the days to its last good day and its standing, caution within 7 days (the owner's choice).

until.description: The last day it is good, YYYY-MM-DD; null for none on record.

solo_xc_determinations.description: 14 CFR 61.93(d)(1)-(3): what an instructor must determine of a solo cross-country themselves before endorsing it (AC 61-65K A.10); (4) and (5) the record answers (endorsement_records).

squawk_meaning.description: What a squawk says, where it says more than a code: 7500 unlawful interference (AIM 6-3-4), 7600 two-way radio failure (AIM 6-4-2), 7700 an emergency (AIM 6-2-2); null for any other.

strip_fuel.description: The fuel figure in the strip at the sheet's foot, web, iPhone and Android alike: the fuel required to the landing of hop `hop` (the first where the route has stops, the tanks filled at each; the whole route's where it has none), less what a flight under way has burnt, never below nothing; and the flights the tanks fall short on, a fuel margin under nothing (14 CFR 91.151, 91.167).

hop.description: The hop flown, 0 where left out.

burnt_gal.description: Burnt so far by a flight under way.

name.description: "C81 → KMSN"; "" for a route with no stops.

sua_altitudes.description: A special-use area's limits in words, STD a flight level (14 CFR 1.1).

mid_sentence.description: Written to go inside a sentence.

taf_window.description: What a TAF says of a window of time: the periods that speak to it (a BECMG lasting past its own window), the worst ceiling and visibility they forecast (TEMPO and PROB included), the prevailing period covering the start, and the prevailing forecast then for its wind (FAA-H-8083-28B 27.4.2.10; BECMG as WMO No. 306 has it).

tafs_along_route.description: The lowest forecast ceiling and visibility among the TAF stations near a route over a window, each station's own worst kept (14 CFR 91.155's cloud clearance is held to them).

temperature_at.description: The temperature at an altitude from a profile: interpolated between levels, past the ends the nearest level's difference from a standard day kept (ICAO standard lapse rate).

terrain_view_bands.description: The pilot's-eye view's colours for the ground under an airplane at `altitude_ft` MSL: amber from `caution_from_ft` (1,000 ft below it), red from `warning_from_ft` (its own altitude), feet MSL; the owner's bands, no regulation's. A picture of the plan, not terrain clearance (no TAWS, TSO-C151; nothing of 14 CFR 91.119 or 91.177).

terrain_way_frame.description: The way round high ground's frame: the grid's corner, cells and samples a cell's side the planner reads the ground at, the highest VFR cruising altitude the airplane reaches either way (14 CFR 91.159, under Class A, 71.33), and the box the fields with fuel are wanted in.

terrain_way_round.description: A way round high ground (route/options/terrain.rs): the fields with fuel and the way's own turns (ident null, for the planner to name off a fix) to fly by, in order, every leg clear of cells whose highest ground with 1,000 ft (14 CFR 91.119) and the coarse read's 1,000 is over the highest cruising altitude the airplane reaches; [] where the straight line is clear, null where there is no way in reach.

tfr_detail_read.description: A TFR's detail from the FAA's TFR XML: its NOTAM, times, altitudes and areas; null where it holds no NOTAM. Not XML is refused.

thin_track.description: At most `most` (4,000 where not given) of `points`, even steps through, the first and last kept; each point as it came.

title_case.description: The FAA's capitals in title case, from text, or each of texts as a list (a null row answers "").

tokens.description: The words heard with each run of figures one number (AIM 4-2-8, 4-2-9).

traffic_fresh.description: Whether each airplane heard is drawn: its position, seen_s old when the answer was made and the answer age_s old now, within 30 s (wingtip.traffic's STALE_S); older, it is somewhere else by now.

traffic_kind.description: An airplane's kind from its ADS-B emitter category (GDL 90 Table 11).

traffic_marks.description: Each airplane's label under it, its height against own ship's in hundreds as TCAS writes it, and whether it is within 1,000 ft of own ship's (14 CFR 91.159), 2,000 ft for an airplane whose height is an uncorrected pressure altitude (pressure_altitude: the two are not on one reference); with own ship's place and the airplane's, how far off it is (nm) and its true bearing from own ship, and tell: near in height and within 5 nm, the traffic the phones notify while the app is not in front (a design choice, no rule).

own_ft.description: Own ship's height above mean sea level, ft, as the phone's GNSS gives it (iOS CLLocation altitude, Android's MSL altitude).

pressure_altitude.description: The airplane's height is its pressure altitude as sent (29.92 "Hg), not set on an altimeter: own_ft is the phone's GNSS above mean sea level, so the near band is 1,000 ft wider for it (PRESSURE_SLACK_FT, about an inch of mercury, FAA-H-8083-25C ch. 11 Figure 11-3).

traffic_matches.description: Whether an airplane heard passes the traffic list's filter.

traffic_pattern.description: The pattern to land on an end (lib/trafficPattern TrafficPattern), or null.

traffic_reach.description: How far round an airport its traffic is asked for, nm: around_nm, about the field (its pattern and one joining it, past 91.117(b)'s 4 nm), and relation_nm, the reach of an airplane inbound or departing, the figures field_relation judges by.

underway.description: Whether own ship moves at flying speed.

vertical_speed.description: The vertical speed in feet a minute from GPS altitudes: the least-squares slope of the last 10 seconds of samples; null with fewer than three of them or under 2 seconds.

vfr_altitudes.description: Every 500 ft from from_ft (1,000 ft where not given), rounded up to a step, to 17,500 ft, the highest VFR cruising altitude under Class A (91.159(a), 71.33(a)): the altitudes a wheel offers.

vfr_basic_minimums.description: The surface-area minimums (14 CFR 91.155(c), (d)), which the planner holds every route to: no VFR under a 1,000 ft ceiling or in under 3 statute miles within a surface area of controlled airspace. Not the least VFR ever asks (Class G at or below 1,200 ft above the surface by day: 1 sm and clear of clouds, 91.155(a)).

vfr_floors.description: The VFR floor of each piece of the route between consecutive breaks: the ground plus 1,000 ft, or a DOF obstacle's top plus 14 CFR 91.119's clearance where it stands (1,000 ft over a congested area, (b); 500 elsewhere, (c); 1,000 where the towns are not known), rounded up to the next 100 ft; with 91.119's own minimum under it.

ground.description: The ground along the direct line, feet MSL; congested null where the towns could not be read.

vfr_minimums.description: 14 CFR 91.155(a)'s basic VFR weather minimums for a class at an altitude MSL (the height above the ground counts in Class G alone, 1,200 ft its line, and is taken as above it where not given): the day's and the night's, or null in Class A, which is flown under IFR (91.135) and begins at 18,000 ft MSL whatever class is asked (71.33).

vfr_not_recommended_reasons.description: "VFR flight not recommended" (AIM 7-1-5) as its reasons, in briefing order: either end reporting IFR or LIFR or a ceiling of unknown height, then the forecast along the route under 14 CFR 91.155(c), (d)'s basic minimums or of unknown height.

vor_check_limit_deg.description: The largest bearing error 14 CFR 91.171 allows for a kind of VOR check: 4 degrees for a test signal (VOT or a repair station's, (b)(1)), a surface checkpoint ((b)(2)) and one receiver against the other ((c)); 6 for an airborne checkpoint ((b)(3)) and a radial along an airway ((b)(4)).

weather_expires_at.description: When a weather report stops counting, Unix seconds UTC, or null where nothing says: a routine METAR an hour after it was observed (AIM 7-1-28, "METAR-hourly"; FMH-1 ch. 2), a SPECI when the next routine report is due, a TAF, the FB winds or an advisory at the end of the valid time its header gives (FAA-H-8083-28B 27.4.1, Table 27-2, 26.2-26.3).

observed.description: When a METAR or SPECI was observed, Unix seconds.

last_routine.description: For a SPECI, the last routine report's time, Unix seconds, where it is known.

valid_to.description: For a forecast, the end of its valid time (the FB winds' FOR USE window), Unix seconds.

weather_held_until.description: To when a stored copy may be served when later fetches fail, by its product's own validity (FAA-H-8083-28B 24.4.1, 26.2-26.3, 27.4.1): METARs no limit, TAFs and SIGMETs to the end of their valid time, PIREPs 90 minutes after the newest, G-AIRMETs 90 minutes after the last snapshot; a copy that says nothing three hours from its fetch. Unix seconds.

weather_in_force.description: Whether a weather report still counts at now: before it expires (weather_expires_at), and, for a forecast, from when its valid time starts, since a TAF's later hours are not today's weather (FAA-H-8083-28B 27.4.1).

now.description: The instant asked about, Unix seconds.

observed.description: When a METAR or SPECI was observed, Unix seconds.

last_routine.description: For a SPECI, the last routine report's time, Unix seconds, where it is known.

valid_from.description: For a forecast, the start of its valid time, Unix seconds.

valid_to.description: For a forecast, the end of its valid time, Unix seconds.

weather_worse.description: What counts as a route's weather getting worse from the briefing the pilot had (then) to a later one (now): a field's METAR in a worse flight category, and worse than VFR (AIM 7-1-7); a SIGMET, AIRMET or G-AIRMET newly on the route (AIM 7-1-6); a TAF where the flight lands forecasting a worse category, and worse than VFR, for the flight's time there; and either with a ceiling of unknown height now (OVC///) where it had a known one, a ceiling not known to be high enough (14 CFR 1.1). A caution, never a limit; each change keyed so an app tells it once.

wind_arrow.description: Whether a field's wind earns its arrow on the map (10 kt or more, or gusting: the owner's pick, 2026-11-10) and whether it warns: its least crosswind more than the airplane's maximum demonstrated crosswind (the POH's, 14 CFR 23.233(a) before amendment 23-64). Never over with no airplane or no figure.

demonstrated_kt.description: The picked airplane's maximum demonstrated crosswind; null with none picked or no figure.

wind_at_altitude.description: The wind at an altitude from a station's levels: interpolated (the direction the short way round), clamped at the ends, light and variable left out; null with no level left, never calm. A list for "altitudes".

levels.description: A station's levels by altitude in feet, as the weather store keeps them.

wind_barb.description: A station model's wind barb: the wind to the nearest 5 kt in flags (50 kt), barbs (10 kt) and half-barbs (5 kt), a circle for calm (FAA-H-8083-28B, 25.2.3.4.5).

wind_calm.description: Whether a wind is calm, a speed of 0 (AIM 7-1-28); no speed is not calm.

wind_components.description: A wind's head- and crosswind on a heading: a tailwind negative, a crosswind from the right positive (the crosswind component chart's figures, FAA-H-8083-25C ch. 11).

wind_pick.description: The wind a field's runways are chosen by (lib/pattern WindPick, AC 90-66C 11.5), or null with no wind to go by.

nearby.description: The nearest report's wind, for a field that reports none (a TAF's, with forecast_at).

ident.description: The end as painted, "" where none is.

variable_kt.description: A variable wind's speed, there only for one.

in_use.description: There only where calm picked the runway in use.

from.description: Where the wind was reported when not at the field.

wind_steady_or_gust.description: The crosswind a wind is judged by, steady or in the gusts, whichever is more, unsigned.

wind_triangle.description: The wind triangle for a true course: the correction (+ right), the true heading and the ground speed; null where no heading holds the course (the wind triangle, FAA-H-8083-25C ch. 16).

words_alt_ft.description: An altitude grouped, "12,500"; an em dash for none (lib/format altFt).

words_ceiling_and_visibility.description: Ceiling and visibility as a briefer says them, "3,500 ft · 6 sm", "no ceiling · —".

words_flight_level.description: A cruising altitude in hundreds of feet, "FL-045"; "FL-___" for none (lib/format flightLevel).

words_grouped.description: A whole number with a comma between each three figures, "12,500" (lib/format grouped).

words_num.description: A number as JavaScript writes it into a string, "null" for none.

words_one.description: A number to a tenth, JavaScript's Math.round(n * 10) / 10.

words_to_fixed.description: JavaScript's toFixed: the nearest, a tie to the larger magnitude, on the float's exact value.

workings_right.description: Whether a student's figure worked on the ground for a leg (ACS PA.I.D, cross-country flight planning) is right within an E6B's accuracy, the drill's own tolerances (the ACS gives none): 2 degrees for the wind correction and the true and magnetic headings (round the compass), 3 kt, 1 min and 0.3 gal.

AheadPolygons.description: An area's outline: polygons, each its outer ring and its holes, each ring [[lon, lat], ...].

AirspaceBand.description: A band of the airspace over a point, as the planner's AirspaceBand: its floor and ceiling in feet MSL, its class, the volume's name for a B, C or D, 91.155(a)'s minimums by day and night (null in Class A), what it takes to go in, the equipment asked (91.215, 91.225) and the 91.117 speed limit.

AltitudeSegment.description: One leg's band: its floor (91.119 under VFR, 91.177(a) under IFR), the ceilings over it, its legal altitudes by its own magnetic course, and what its floor was found from.

ApproachAttempt.title: ApproachAttempt
ApproachAttempt.description: An attempt at an approach as indices into the track's points: where it crossed the final approach fix inbound, and the points it runs from and to.

ApproachDebrief.title: ApproachDebrief

faf_at.description: When the track crossed the final approach fix inbound, ms.

fit_nm.description: How far off the final it flew on average, nm.

glidepath_fit_ft.description: How far off the glidepath on average, ft, where there is one.

under_ft.description: Its furthest under its minimum on the way to it, ft (+ under).

crossings.description: The fixes passed in order (AIM 5-4-5), the missed approach's left out.

lowest_ft.description: The lowest after the final approach fix, before the missed approach point (14 CFR 91.175(c), (e)).

also_fits.description: Approaches whose final the track fitted as well, by name.

ApproachDebrief.description: One attempt at an approach debriefed (the web's ApproachDebrief, snake_case): off the course past full scale (AIM 1-1-9, 1-1-17), each fix's crossing (AIM 5-4-5), the lowest against the pilot's minimums (14 CFR 91.175(c), (e)).

ApproachFacts.title: ApproachFacts

threshold_ft.description: The landing threshold's elevation, ft MSL (the CIFP's runway record, ARINC 424-18 5.68).

tdze_ft.description: The touchdown zone elevation, ft MSL, to a tenth (NASR APT_RWY_END TDZ_ELEV).

code.description: The fix's altitude description (ARINC 424-18 5.29): "G" or "H" the glide slope's altitude at the FAF, "I" or "J" its intercept altitude at the FACF, "V" the vertical path's at a step-down fix.

ft.description: That altitude, ft MSL: the record's second altitude.

levels.description: The levels of service the CIFP authorises (ARINC 424-19 5.275, 5.276): "LPV", "LNAV/VNAV", "LNAV", ...

ApproachFacts.description: What the CIFP says of an approach besides its legs (wingtip.approach_facts): its runway, the altitudes coded beside a fix's limits, and the levels of service authorised.

minimums.description: The minimums' finding, put in again as the pilot types theirs; written only when true.

ApproachFixTag.title: ApproachFixTag

altitude.description: How the fix is crossed (ARINC 424-18 5.29): at min_ft (= max_ft), at or above min_ft, at or below max_ft, or between them; the FAA charts at or above underlined, at or below overlined.

kind.description: An ILS's electronic glide slope ("GS") or an RNAV approach's glidepath ("GP").

ft.description: Its altitude at the FAF, ft MSL.

source.description: "cifp" the CIFP's own (ARINC 424-18 5.29 "G"/"H"); "computed" from the angle, threshold and TCH by FAA Order 8260.3G formula 2-6-4.

vertical.description: At the final approach fix of an ILS, or of an RNAV approach with LPV or LNAV/VNAV minimums.

tdze_ft.description: Whole feet, as the plate prints it.

runway.description: At a missed approach point that is the runway: its threshold elevation, threshold crossing height and touchdown zone elevation. No DA or MDA: those are the plate's alone.

ApproachFixTag.description: One fix's tag on the map with its approach's plate.

ApproachRunwayPath.title: ApproachRunwayPath
ApproachRunwayPath.description: The glidepath placed on its runway: its threshold, the height it crosses it at and its angle.

BestField.title: BestField
BestField.description: One field ranked by best_fields, with its reasons.

heading_true_deg.description: The heading to fly there, wind corrected; null where the airspeed is not known.

heading_mag_deg.description: The same, magnetic; null without variation_deg.

reach.description: within: over the field at pattern height (1,000 ft, AC 90-66C) or more; low: there, under it; unknown: no glide figures, altitude or elevation, or a diversion.

reach_nm.description: How far the glide goes over the ground along the course, wind corrected.

arrive_agl_ft.description: Height over the field on arrival.

runway.description: The end to land on: the POH's distance fits, the crosswind within the demonstrated, the most headwind, the most nearly straight in, the longest.

needed_ft.description: The POH's short-field landing over 50 ft in the field's air.

CircuitRunwayIn.title: CircuitRunwayIn

traffic.description: "right" for right traffic; anything else, or none, is left (14 CFR 91.126(b)(1)).

CircuitRunwayIn.description: A runway as the traffic pattern draws it: its ends' idents, true headings, traffic and thresholds.

ClassBShelf.description: A Class B shelf other than the flight's own (whose surface area holds one of its ends), as the FAA's Class Airspace shapefile has it: its floor and ceiling, ft MSL, and its rings of [lat, lon].
ClassBShelf.title: ClassBShelf

kind.description: Anything else is read as not known.

said.description: Words naming one place or more, to be found.

CoachDebrief.title: CoachDebrief
CoachDebrief.description: One of the pilot's own debriefed flights, trimmed to what proficiency_plan reads.

kind.description: An approach debriefed (route's approach_debrief) or a flight against its plan (debrief).

place.description: Where: the approach's field, or the flight's route ("KMSN-KJVL").

procedure.description: An approach's procedure as the chart names it ("ILS Y RWY 08"); none for a flight.

elevation_ft.description: The field's elevation, ft MSL, for the 500 ft gate (AC 61-98D 2.1.4); without it the gate is not checked.

off.description: Past full scale, or under a minimum, there.

profile.description: An approach's profile.track as its debrief gives it.

findings.description: An approach debrief's findings, as worded.

off_ft.description: Its altitude less pattern altitude, ft (+ high).

CopilotAlternative.title: CopilotAlternative
CopilotAlternative.description: The best alternative: best_fields' first diversion pick that the copilot's weather and fuel checks find good.

raw.description: The report as sent, which copilot_watch reads its category and ceiling from (metar::parse); without it the field has no weather.

planned_category.description: Its flight category when the copilot first saw it, so a worse one is said as a change.

CopilotField.title: CopilotField
CopilotField.description: A candidate as best_fields reads it, with fuel and the category first seen: /api/copilot/around's.

id.description: The same while what it says is; speak a message once by it.

elsewhere.description: Drawn by the alerts-ahead banner, not the copilot's.

level.description: "check": outside what light airplanes' handbooks give, or at odds with another figure; "wrong": cannot be right as read.

field.description: The figure it is about where it is one: a logbook entry's member ("nightHours").

says.description: What to check, a sentence the pilot reads.

EndHeadings.title: EndHeadings
EndHeadings.description: A runway's ends as [ident, true heading], either null.

FieldFrequency.title: FieldFrequency
FieldFrequency.description: A field's frequency as the planner sends it (NASR's type code, description and MHz).

type.description: NASR's code: TWR, GND, ATIS, CTAF, UNICOM...

FieldHour.title: FieldHour
FieldHour.description: One hour of a field's weather for the airport card: Now from the METAR, then each whole hour its TAF covers (FAA-H-8083-28B 27.4.2.10's change groups).

at.description: The hour's start, ms; Now's the report's time (or now).

at_times.description: A TEMPO's or PROB's category this hour where worse than the prevailing one.

at_times_chance.description: The worse weather at times comes only from a PROB group (FAA-H-8083-28B 27.4.2.10.3).

FuelField.description: A public field as NASR's APT_BASE has it (its ICAO ident where it has one, and the FAA's), with what fuel it sells and its longest open paved runway (OurAirports' runways).
FuelField.title: FuelField

FuelStop.description: A field to land at for fuel: its miles from the flight's departure and those it adds to the straight line, the fuel left on landing and the minutes flown to it.
FuelStop.title: FuelStop

GonogoAlternateData.title: GonogoAlternateData

required.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

good.description: False: under its alternate minimums; null: the pilot's to check; left out: says nothing.

GonogoAlternateData.description: The planner's /api/alternate answer, as much as the finding reads.

caveats.description: What could not be had from the table: beyond its altitudes or temperatures, heavier than its heaviest weight, a tailwind past the POH's figures, or no wind correction in the airplane's profile.

why.description: The rule or the reason it counts.

stop.description: Makes the flight unlawful as planned: high, whatever the points.

group.description: A self check's group; left out for the others.

finding.description: Its mark; null for a self check.

GonogoFlown.title: GonogoFlown
GonogoFlown.description: The runway and end flown, by index, or null.

GonogoInspections.title: GonogoInspections
GonogoInspections.description: The airplane's inspections and tests as its owner recorded them; null or a member left out says nothing.

GonogoItem.title: GonogoItem

tab.description: The planning panel's tab that shows it in full.

section.description: The section of that tab, by its title.

finding.description: "ok", "caution", "stop", "unknown" or "pending"; "" for a risk level not known (verdict::risk_finding).

GonogoItem.description: One tab's finding and where it is shown in full.

GonogoLine.title: GonogoLine
GonogoLine.description: What the findings come to, in a line over them.

stations_lb.description: Each station's load, in the loading's station order.

GonogoLoading.title: GonogoLoading

envelope.description: The CG envelope's points, [arm in, weight lb].

GonogoLoading.description: A profile's loading: limits, stations, fuel and envelope.

GonogoMetar.title: GonogoMetar
GonogoMetar.description: A field's METAR, as much as the rules read of it.

GonogoPicks.title: GonogoPicks

pattern.description: Field to end, as an object or [field, end] pairs.

takeoff.description: Field to end, as an object or [field, end] pairs.

GonogoPicks.description: The pilot's picked runway ends, landing (pattern) and takeoff.

vfr_not_recommended.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

tfr_on_route.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

hazards.description: The number of SIGMETs and G-AIRMETs on the route.

night.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

night_passengers.description: Whether any of the flight is in 14 CFR 61.57(b)'s period, 1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise (passenger_night_on_the_way), its own window rather than 1.1's night; left out or null, `night` stands for it.

ifr.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

within_limit.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

vor_check.description: The VOR check (14 CFR 91.171): left out for a stock profile, null for none recorded.

inoperative.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

instrument_current_from.description: pilot_currency's instrumentCurrentFrom: before this day the pilot is not instrument current yet.

ticked.description: The self checks ticked, by key, true where ticked.

GonogoRunwayWind.title: GonogoRunwayWind

in_use.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

GonogoRunwayWind.description: The planner's RunwayWind on a runway.

over_obstacle.description: Total over a 50 ft obstacle, in distance_unit.

words.description: The words on the page the figure was read from.

HeardPlane.title: HeardPlane
HeardPlane.description: An airplane as the map's traffic draws it, the planner's TrafficAircraft (wingtip.traffic): who, where, how high, its track, speed and climb, how old.

num.description: The run of figures said as one number, as digits; left out where the word is no figure.

names.description: The field's instrument approach charts (IAP) by their d-TPP names, "ILS OR LOC RWY 27", "RNAV (GPS) RWY 9"; the engine decides which are precision (precision_approach: ILS, GLS, PAR, AIM 5-4-5 a.7(a)).

approaches.description: The field's instrument approaches as the d-TPP lists them: their names, and its nonstandard alternate minimums page.

covers.description: taf_window's worst.covers: whether the TAF covers the whole window. Missing is taken as not.

forecast.description: The worst its TAF forecasts over the window (taf_window's worst, with its `covers`), null where the field has no TAF or none says anything of the window.

KeptKind.title: KeptKind
KeptKind.description: A kind of answer the apps keep for the air: the briefing, the route's METARs and TAFs, the ranked NOTAMs, the route's airport cards, the destination's and alternate's plates, the plan with its nav log, the Go / No-Go and the weather loop's frame list.

LessonFocus.title: LessonFocus
LessonFocus.description: What a lesson's step shows on the map: a fix ringed, a part of the procedure's line drawn over.

LogbookEntry.description: The gateway's LogbookEntry, camelCase: the columns the currency and 61.109 rules read. A column missing or null is none of it.

dayLandings.description: Every landing, by day or at night (61.57(a)).

nightLandings.description: Landings to a full stop at night (61.57(b)).

passenger_night.description: 61.57(b)'s period, 1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise.

counts_night.description: To a full stop in 61.57(b)'s period.

passenger_night.description: 61.57(b)'s period, 1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise.

MetarWindIn.title: MetarWindIn
MetarWindIn.description: A METAR's wind; null, missing or empty for none.

NavLogAirAt.title: NavLogAirAt
NavLogAirAt.description: A leg's air at one altitude, looked up at its midpoint: no wind is no winds-aloft station near, no temperature a standard day.

NavLogFigure.title: NavLogFigure
NavLogFigure.description: The route flown at one altitude for the altitude wheel: each leg at it where legal, else at its nearest legal one.

NavLogLeg.title: NavLogLeg

start_at.description: A pilot's Start At at the fix the leg starts from (wingtip.own_altitude): a descent to the leg's lower altitude begins at that fix and runs on from it at three to one, rather than being done by it (navlog_with_descents).

NavLogLeg.description: A nav log leg (PHAK ch. 16's dead reckoning); null time, ground speed and fuel is an unflyable leg. Members the log does not know (procedure, hold, airway) are carried through.

NavLogProfile.title: NavLogProfile

cruise_tas_kt.description: At its cruise power at cruise_altitude_ft (else 6,000 ft) on a standard day.

NavLogProfile.description: An airplane's profile (data/aircraft/*.json, a pilot's own figures laid over it). A figure of 0 is taken as none.

NavLogRow.title: NavLogRow

kind.description: "fix" for a fix flown through rather than a field.

anyOf.description: The planner's Leg (/api/plan), as it comes.
The piece of the leg that arrives at this row, where a top of climb or descent cuts it.

NavLogRow.description: A nav log row, the web's NavLogRow: its place is the checkpoint's (cp), the top of climb's or descent's (point) or the airport's.

NavLogSegment.title: NavLogSegment
NavLogSegment.description: The altitude selection's segment for a leg: its legal altitudes (14 CFR 91.119, 91.159, the airspace, the clouds and the service ceiling).

NavLogTop.title: NavLogTop
NavLogTop.description: A top of climb (toc) or descent (tod): its miles, minutes and gallons into the leg.

NavLogWind.title: NavLogWind
NavLogWind.description: The wind aloft, the direction it blows from in true degrees, carried onto the leg as it is.

OwnShipFix.title: OwnShipFix
OwnShipFix.description: Own ship as the GPS has it.

PracticePlace.title: PracticePlace
PracticePlace.description: A field near the pilot's home, as the host found it in its data.

lighted.description: A lighted runway (NASR), for night landings.

precision.description: Has an electronic glidepath by its name: an ILS or a GLS.

ProcedureDrawing.title: ProcedureDrawing
ProcedureDrawing.description: A procedure as the planner draws it from the FAA's CIFP (/api/procedure's answer as it comes); only the members the engine reads.

until.description: The last day it is good, YYYY-MM-DD; null with nothing on record.

from.description: A currency not begun yet: its first day (61.57(c)(1)'s month after).

days_left.description: Days from today to until; negative where lapsed.

detail.description: What it takes, in a sentence, with its rule.

key.description: The currency ("night_passengers", "ipc") or weak area ("unstable_approach") it answers.

practise.description: What to practise, with its source.

why.description: The ids it answers: "due:<key>" and evidence ids.

place.description: The nearest field suited to it; null where any will do or none was given.

minutes.description: The plan's suggestion of its length, not a rule.

wings.description: Where it may count toward a WINGS flight activity; never a claim that it does.

ReadyItem.title: ReadyItem

key.description: route, airplane, altitude, charts, packs, briefing, fields, notams, saved, location, battery or receiver.

finding.description: Never a stop: warn, never limit.

line.description: One line a pilot acts on.

source.description: Where its limit comes from: the FAA schedule, the CFR section, the AIM paragraph, or the app's choice.

fix.description: What the app does in place for it; null where nothing on the device fixes it.

ReadyItem.description: One thing ready_to_fly checked: whether it is fine, a line to act on and the fix done in place.

ReceiverBlock.title: ReceiverBlock
ReceiverBlock.description: A FIS-B NEXRAD block (products 63 regional and 64 CONUS): 32 bins across and 4 down, north row first, each a level 0 to 7.

bins.description: 128 digits 0 to 7, row by row from the north-west.

ReceiverNexradLevel.title: ReceiverNexradLevel
ReceiverNexradLevel.description: One NEXRAD level's rectangles, [south, west, north, east] degrees each.

ReceiverOwnship.title: ReceiverOwnship
ReceiverOwnship.description: Own ship as the receiver's GPS gives it.

hex.description: The address as the internet's traffic writes it: six lower-case hex digits, a ~ before one that is not an ICAO address.

address_type.description: 0 ADS-B with an ICAO address, 1 ADS-B self-assigned, 2 TIS-B ICAO, 3 TIS-B track file, 4 surface vehicle, 5 ground station beacon (GDL 90 3.5.1.2).

track_kind.description: True track, true heading or magnetic heading (GDL 90 3.5.1.5).

category.description: DO-260B's emitter category, A1 light to C5 line obstacle.

emergency.description: 0 none, 1 general, 2 medical, 3 minimum fuel, 4 no communication, 5 unlawful interference, 6 downed aircraft (GDL 90 3.5.1.12).

at.description: When it was last heard, Unix s.

geometric_ft.description: The GPS height (GDL 90 ID 11), ft: above MSL where the receiver says so (receiver.msl), else above the WGS-84 ellipsoid.

vfom_m.description: Its Vertical Figure of Merit, m.

ReceiverPicture.title: ReceiverPicture
ReceiverPicture.description: What a receiver has said so far: hand it back with the next bytes.

name.description: The name its ID message gives (Stratux, Sentry, SkyEcho).

live.description: A Heartbeat came in the last 5 s (one a second, GDL 90 3.1).

summary.description: One line for the receiver's chip: "Stratux · 12 targets · GPS".

msl.description: Its GPS heights are above MSL (ForeFlight's ID message), else the ellipsoid.

bad_frames.description: Frames whose CRC did not match, dropped.

ReceiverReport.title: ReceiverReport
ReceiverReport.description: A field's report as FIS-B sent it: its kind (METAR, SPECI, TAF), its words as sent, the product's time HHMMZ and when it was last heard, Unix s.

ReceiverTarget.title: ReceiverTarget
ReceiverTarget.description: An airplane a receiver reports (GDL 90's Traffic or Ownship Report, 560-1058-00 Rev A 3.5.1), as heard.

hex.description: The address as the internet's traffic writes it: six lower-case hex digits, a ~ before one that is not an ICAO address.

address_type.description: 0 ADS-B with an ICAO address, 1 ADS-B self-assigned, 2 TIS-B ICAO, 3 TIS-B track file, 4 surface vehicle, 5 ground station beacon (GDL 90 3.5.1.2).

track_kind.description: True track, true heading or magnetic heading (GDL 90 3.5.1.5).

category.description: DO-260B's emitter category, A1 light to C5 line obstacle.

emergency.description: 0 none, 1 general, 2 medical, 3 minimum fuel, 4 no communication, 5 unlawful interference, 6 downed aircraft (GDL 90 3.5.1.12).

at.description: When it was last heard, Unix s.

ReceiverText.title: ReceiverText
ReceiverText.description: A FIS-B text product as sent (AIM 4-5-9): a METAR, TAF, winds aloft or PIREP (product 413), or a NOTAM, TFR, AIRMET, SIGMET, SUA status, G-AIRMET or CWA text record.

kind.description: METAR, SPECI, TAF, WINDS, PIREP ... or NOTAM, AIRMET, SIGMET, SUA, G-AIRMET, CWA, NOTAM-TRA, NOTAM-TMOA.

text.description: The words as sent; a METAR or TAF without its kind, as the METAR and TAF readers take it.

at.description: When it was last sent, Unix s.

RecentWindIn.title: RecentWindIn
RecentWindIn.description: The field's last wind, for a calm one; both members needed where it is not empty.

RouteHold.title: RouteHold
RouteHold.description: A pilot's hold as the route's address writes it ("VPBNG/090/30:270:R:1M:2T"): legs by minutes or by nm, length by turns or by minutes, the other of each pair null.

fix.description: The point held at: an airport, a fix, or the pilot's own point off one.

inbound.description: The inbound course to the fix, magnetic degrees, 0 to 359.

leg_min.description: The legs in minutes, or null where they are in nm.

leg_nm.description: The legs in nm, or null where they are in minutes.

turns.description: Laps to fly, or null where held by minutes.

minutes.description: Minutes to hold, or null where held by turns.

RouteHoldIn.title: RouteHoldIn
RouteHoldIn.description: A hold as the engine takes one: exactly one of leg_min and leg_nm, and (to write it) exactly one of whole turns and minutes.

RouteOption.description: One way: its kind and every kind it is the best of, its points between the ends (fixes, points of the pilot's own, fuel stops), the fuel stops among them and those with somewhere to eat, its path, distance, minutes in the air and on the ground (30 a landing), fuel, landings, the hazards it crosses and the marginal ones it passes (indices into hazards), and what it meets. With no airplane (a null profile) its minutes in the air and its fuel are null, and it has no fuel stops.
RouteOption.title: RouteOption

RouteOptionsAdvisory.description: A SIGMET (valid_from, valid_to) or a G-AIRMET (valid, its snapshot), its area as [lat, lon] points, as the AWC sends it.
RouteOptionsAdvisory.title: RouteOptionsAdvisory

RouteOptionsAlong.description: What a way meets: its weather as runs by the minutes they last, the mean wind along it (positive a tailwind), its floor (the highest ground with 14 CFR 91.119's 1,000 ft) and its miles out of glide of dry land.
RouteOptionsAlong.title: RouteOptionsAlong

RouteOptionsArea.description: A special-use area (type P, R, MOA, W, A ...) or a TFR in force (notam_id, title): its rings of [lat, lon], an odd number of them holding a point inside.
RouteOptionsArea.title: RouteOptionsArea

RouteOptionsField.description: A public field selling 100LL (NASR APT_BASE), its longest open paved runway and whether there is somewhere to eat (null: not read yet).
RouteOptionsField.title: RouteOptionsField

RouteOptionsFix.description: A fix as the planner reads it (wingtip.fixes): a navaid with its own magnetic variation (east positive), a VFR waypoint or any other.
RouteOptionsFix.title: RouteOptionsFix

profile.description: The airplane; missing or null for none picked: the ways are then costed in still air, with no minutes, fuel or fuel stops.

night.description: Night at either end (14 CFR 91.151's 45 minutes) as the host judged it; missing or null, the engine judges it over the flight's window (sun.rs).

RouteOptionsReport.description: A field's weather: a TAF (its worst over the flight, with the weather of every group then) or a METAR.
RouteOptionsReport.title: RouteOptionsReport

RouteOptionsStation.description: An FD station and its wind [from true, kt] at each of the frame's altitudes_ft, null where it gives none.
RouteOptionsStation.title: RouteOptionsStation

Runway.title: Runway

closed.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

Runway.description: A runway as the planner sends one.

RunwayWindOut.title: RunwayWindOut

in_use.description: There only where calm picked the runway in use.

RunwayWindOut.description: The planner's RunwayWind: the end the wind favours and its components, whole numbers where the wind blew, 0 where calm; null for none.

ShortFieldTable.title: ShortFieldTable

tables.description: One per weight, each a grid of altitudes by temperatures.

headwind_kt_per_10pct.description: The POH's note to the chart: the knots of headwind that take 10% off the distances. Null or missing: no correction for a headwind.

tailwind_kt_per_10pct.description: The POH's note to the chart: the knots of tailwind that add 10% to the distances. Null or missing: no correction, and a caveat with a tailwind.

tailwind_max_kt.description: The strongest tailwind the POH gives figures for, kt; past it a caveat.

ShortFieldTable.description: A POH's short-field takeoff or landing table: at least two altitudes and two temperatures, a grid of them for every weight.

TafPeriod.title: TafPeriod
TafPeriod.description: One period of a TAF as the weather store keeps it (awc_tafs_read): Unix seconds, the change group ("", FM, BECMG, TEMPO, PROB), the wind from true north, and the ceiling (14 CFR 1.1) and visibility (statute miles).

TrafficPatternOut.title: TrafficPatternOut
TrafficPatternOut.description: lib/trafficPattern's TrafficPattern in snake_case, or null where it cannot be drawn.

TrafficPlane.title: TrafficPlane

seen_s.description: How old its position is, s.

TrafficPlane.description: An airplane as the traffic feed sends it: what the rules read of it.

VerdictInput.title: VerdictInput

pending.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

vfr_not_recommended.description: AIM 7-1-5's "VFR flight not recommended", its reasons.

icing.description: Icing possible at an altitude flown, in a line (gonogo_icing).

hazards.description: SIGMETs and G-AIRMETs along the route, by name.

unchecked.description: Sources that did not answer, by name.

worst.description: The worst the forecast says along the route, in words.

terminal_alerts.description: ITWS alerts in force now at the route's airports, each in its words with its airport (AIM 4-3-7).

flow_programs.description: The Command Center's ground stops and delay programs at the route's airports, in words; a finding under IFR only.

ifr.description: The flight is planned IFR. Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

pending.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

in_force.description: TFRs on the route in force when the flight gets there.

near.description: The number of TFRs near the route not in force.

when.description: gonogo_sua_when's answer, or SFDPS's status now: active-now, cold-now.

pending.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

problem.description: No VFR altitude fits, in a line.

flown.description: The altitude flown as the FL chip says it.

pending.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

margin_gal.description: The least the tanks hold over the fuel and its reserve; null where usable fuel is not known.

ifr.description: Under IFR the reserve is 14 CFR 91.167's, not 91.151's.

pending.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

worked.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

beyond.description: Fields whose distances were read past the POH's table: a caution.

unchecked.description: Fields whose distances could not be held to the runway (its length or the field's elevation not known): unknown, never ok.

pending.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

worked.description: Read as JavaScript reads it: missing, null, false, 0 and "" are false.

VerdictInput.description: The web's VerdictInput: each tab's say, and the risk assessment's level and line (null while the briefing is awaited).

VfrMinimumsRule.description: A row of 14 CFR 91.155(a)'s table: the flight visibility in statute miles and the distance from clouds in feet (all three null: clear of clouds), and the row as the drill words it.

WeatherReading.title: WeatherReading
WeatherReading.description: One reading of a route's weather: the METARs of its fields, the advisories near it and the TAFs for the flight's time at each field.

WeatherWorseItem.title: WeatherWorseItem
WeatherWorseItem.description: One way the weather got worse.

key.description: The change and its new state ("metar:KMSN:IFR", "advisory:<key>", "taf:KDLH:MVFR", "metar:KMSN:ceiling-unknown"): an app tells a key once.

line.description: The change in a pilot's words: "KMSN is IFR now; it was VFR at the briefing".

WeatherWorst.title: WeatherWorst
WeatherWorst.description: The worst a TAF forecasts in a window, TEMPO and PROB groups included, and whether the TAF covers the whole window.

covers.description: Whether the prevailing periods (the first line and each FM) cover the whole window without a gap: a TAF ending or beginning inside it says nothing of the rest (14 CFR 91.169(b)(2)(i)).

WordingStation.title: WordingStation
WordingStation.description: A VOR as the planner sends one; with no mag_var it gives no radials.

mag_var.description: The station's magnetic variation, degrees east.

WorseAdvisory.title: WorseAdvisory
WorseAdvisory.description: A SIGMET, AIRMET or G-AIRMET in one reading (AIM 7-1-6).

key.description: What names the advisory from one reading to the next: its text as sent, or its hazard, severity and altitudes.

kind.description: "SIGMET", "Convective SIGMET", "AIRMET" or "G-AIRMET", as the app words it.

on_route.description: Whether the briefing places it on the route.

WorseField.title: WorseField
WorseField.description: A field's ceiling and visibility in one reading: its METAR's, or its TAF's for the flight's time there. The engine reads the flight category (AIM 7-1-7).

ceiling_unknown.description: The lowest broken, overcast or obscured layer sent with no height (14 CFR 1.1): not known, not none.

arrival.description: A TAF where the flight lands (a stop or the destination): only those are compared.
